snapshot.stmt:
There is a positive, fully explicit triangle witness.  Let \(n=3\), let
\[
G=\begin{bmatrix}0&1&1\\1&0&1\\1&1&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\nu(w)=\left(\frac13\right)^{\sum_iw_i}
       \left(\frac23\right)^{3-\sum_iw_i},
\]
and, writing \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\), define
\[
f_i(w)=
\begin{cases}
1,&w_i=1\text{ and }w_j=w_k=0,\\
0,&w_i=0\text{ and }w_j+w_k\ge1,\\
\star,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(J_3=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}\) and \(A=(I_3+J_3)/4\), the exact design and endpoint inputs are
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad c_U=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(c_L)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For normalized representatives \(B(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}x&0\\0&y\end{bmatrix}\), the full optimizer correspondences are
\[
\mathcal A_0=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=\mathbf 1^{\top}y=x^{\top}y=0
\right\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,\ 
(\mathbf 1^{\top}y)^2=\frac{216}{55}
\right\}.
\]
They are nonempty, and their exact objective values satisfy
\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad
w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200}\quad(B_0\in\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432}
\quad(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}).
\]
Moreover every member of \(\mathcal A_0\cup\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) obeys
\[
\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=\frac4{27}.
\]
Consequently \(\xi_0=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\), and the rational choices
\[
\delta=\frac{4912}{39525},
\qquad
\eta=\frac5{216}
\]
give the full-correspondence certificates
\[
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_0)
-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=\delta>0
\]
and
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\left\{\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\right\}
=\eta>0.
\]

Endpoint covariances alone do not determine the minimax worst-copula residual value.  In particular, let \(n=3\), let \(W_1,W_2,W_3\) be independent Bernoulli \(1/2\) variables under \(\nu\), and set \(f_i(w)=w_i\). \qquad c_L=c_U=0,
\]

\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\frac1{36}.
\]

\[

\qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon.
\]

Endpoint covariances alone do not determine the minimax worst-copula residual value.  In particular, let \(n=3\), let \(W_1,W_2,W_3\) be independent Bernoulli \(1/2\) variables under \(\nu\), and set \(f_i(w)=w_i\).  With \(\kappa=1/8\) and \(\varepsilon=1/100\), the marginal pairs \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_0,\delta_0)\) and \((F_1,F_0)=(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),\delta_0)\) produce the same moment-incomplete tuple
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12 I_6,\qquad
\Omega=\tfrac14\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix},
\qquad c_L=c_U=0,
\]
but their endpoint moment matrices differ and their minimax residual values are, respectively,
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\frac1{36}.
\]
Consequently, no algorithm whose only input is \((\Pi,\Omega,c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon)\) can always return rational bounds
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon.
\]
Thus endpoint moment matrices such as \(Q(c_L)\) and \(Q(c_U)\), or equivalent marginal moments, are necessary inputs for the proposed certification problem.  This obstruction makes no claim that the corrected moment-complete branch-and-bound solver terminates at every positive tolerance.

\end{bmatrix},

\[

\right\}.

\[

\qquad

\[

\[

snapshot.stmt:
For every rational signed pivot-chart box, intersection with the normalized feasible set \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is an existential semialgebraic question.  More explicitly, sphere feasibility, chart and box restrictions, and \(S_B-n\kappa I_2\succeq0\) are finitely many polynomial equalities and weak inequalities with rational or real-algebraic coefficients; for
\[
 S_B-n\kappa I_2=\begin{bmatrix}u&v\\v&z\end{bmatrix},
\]
the matrix inequality is exactly \(u\ge0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(uz-v^2\ge0\).  Cylindrical algebraic decomposition therefore terminates with either an exact real-algebraic feasible sample or a finite infeasibility certificate, including when feasibility occurs only on the equality boundary.

\[

\]
For every \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\) and every \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\),
\[
 g_{\iota(B)}^+(c)=g_B(c),

\[

\]
where \(P_B\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(Z_B)\), \(A_e\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(P_B)=\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}\).  On rank two, \([B]_+=\iota([C])\) for a unique \([C]\in\mathcal B_Z\), and the gains and losses agree. \[
 L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
 \qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
The incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\) has finite real-algebraic coordinates, including when every feasible point lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  The checker verifies only CAD sign certificates, algebraic feasibility, outward objective bounds, rational norm and diameter records, chart cover, pruning inequalities, and mesh; the displayed facts about \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) are mathematical consequences.  Along every \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and meshes converge to zero.  No uniform complexity bound or semidefinite-program reduction is asserted.

defs.def:branch-bound-handle: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions, optionally tightened by interval-Hessian underestimators.  For any chart box whose feasible intersection is nonempty, repeated bisection and exact feasible-child selection produce nested closed feasible boxes with diameters tending to zero; their singleton intersection supplies the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible incumbent authorized by the certificate definition.  The procedure prunes only by exact infeasibility or by a certified box lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound, and it refines the finite quotient-chart cover and arithmetic enclosures until \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\) and \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), at which point it returns the full certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\).

\[
f_i(w)=
\begin{cases}
1,&w_i=1\text{ and }w_j=w_k=0,\\
0,&w_i=0\text{ and }w_j+w_k\ge1,\\
\star,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(J_3=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}\) and \(A=(I_3+J_3)/4\), the exact inputs are

\qquad

68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},

\qquad

\qquad

\[

\ \mathbf1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,

\quad w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200},

\[

defs.def:branch-bound-handle: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions, optionally tightened by interval-Hessian underestimators.  For any chart box whose feasible intersection is nonempty, repeated bisection and exact feasible-child selection produce nested closed feasible boxes with diameters tending to zero; their singleton intersection supplies the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible incumbent authorized by the certificate definition.  The procedure prunes only by exact infeasibility or by a certified box lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound, and it refines the finite quotient-chart cover and arithmetic enclosures until \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\) and \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), at which point it returns the full certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\).

snapshot.stmt:
Endpoint covariances alone do not determine the minimax worst-copula residual value.  In particular, let \(n=3\), let \(W_1,W_2,W_3\) be independent Bernoulli \(1/2\) variables under \(\nu\), and set \(f_i(w)=w_i\).  With \(\kappa=1/8\) and \(\varepsilon=1/100\), the marginal pairs \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_0,\delta_0)\) and \((F_1,F_0)=(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),\delta_0)\) produce the same moment-incomplete tuple
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12 I_6,\qquad
\Omega=\tfrac14\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix},
\qquad c_L=c_U=0,
\]
but their endpoint moment matrices differ and their minimax residual values are, respectively,
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\frac1{36}.
\]
Consequently, no algorithm whose only input is \((\Pi,\Omega,c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon)\) can always return rational bounds
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon.
\]
Thus endpoint moment matrices such as \(Q(c_L)\) and \(Q(c_U)\), or equivalent marginal moments, are necessary inputs for the proposed certification problem.  This obstruction makes no claim that the corrected moment-complete branch-and-bound solver terminates at every positive tolerance.

Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\). For every moment-complete input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying exposure positivity and \(\kappa\)-feasibility, and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), the candidate projective interval branch-and-bound procedure terminates after finitely many subdivisions and returns a checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad
U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
Here \(B_{\varepsilon}\in\mathcal B_\kappa\) is represented exactly, including when the feasible set has no relative interior and lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  A chart box meeting that equality boundary is never discarded as infeasible; it may be discarded only when its certified objective lower bound exceeds the incumbent upper bound.  Consequently, along any sequence \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and retained-box mesh diameters converge to zero.  This is a finite, instance-dependent termination result; it asserts neither a uniform complexity bound nor a semidefinite-program reduction.

defs.def:branch-bound-handle: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions, optionally tightened by interval-Hessian underestimators.  For any chart box whose feasible intersection is nonempty, repeated bisection and exact feasible-child selection produce nested closed feasible boxes with diameters tending to zero; their singleton intersection supplies the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible incumbent authorized by the certificate definition.  The procedure prunes only by exact infeasibility or by a certified box lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound, and it refines the finite quotient-chart cover and arithmetic enclosures until \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\) and \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), at which point it returns the full certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\).

There is a positive, fully explicit triangle witness.  Let \(n=3\), let
\[
G=\begin{bmatrix}0&1&1\\1&0&1\\1&1&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\nu(w)=\left(\frac13\right)^{\sum_iw_i}
       \left(\frac23\right)^{3-\sum_iw_i},
\]
and, writing \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\), define
\[
f_i(w)=
\begin{cases}
1,&w_i=1\text{ and }w_j=w_k=0,\\
0,&w_i=0\text{ and }w_j+w_k\ge1,\\
\star,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(J_3=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}\) and \(A=(I_3+J_3)/4\), the exact design and endpoint inputs are
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad c_U=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(c_L)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For normalized representatives \(B(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}x&0\\0&y\end{bmatrix}\), the full optimizer correspondences are
\[
\mathcal A_0=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=\mathbf 1^{\top}y=x^{\top}y=0
\right\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,\ 
(\mathbf 1^{\top}y)^2=\frac{216}{55}
\right\}.
\]
They are nonempty, and their exact objective values satisfy
\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad
w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200}\quad(B_0\in\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432}
\quad(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}).
\]
Moreover every member of \(\mathcal A_0\cup\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) obeys
\[
\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=\frac4{27}.
\]
Consequently \(\xi_0=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\), and the rational choices
\[
\delta=\frac{4912}{39525},
\qquad
\eta=\frac5{216}
\]
give the full-correspondence certificates
\[
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_0)
-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=\delta>0
\]
and
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\left\{\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\right\}
=\eta>0.
\]

snapshot.stmt: Under ass:known-exposure, ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, ass:exposure-positivity, and ass:iid-potential-pairs, every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) has affine functions \(c\mapsto g_B(c)\) and \(c\mapsto\ell_B(c)\) on the imported feasible domain \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\). Consequently, \(\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}\ell_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\), with both extrema attained. The product coupling gives \(c_L\le0\le c_U\), so \(g_B(0)\) is an ordinarily typed feasible-covariance gain. If \(c_L<0<c_U\), \(g_B(0)=\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})\) if and only if the affine slope of \(g_B\) is zero.

defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.

assumptions.ass:exposure-positivity: For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
assumptions.ass:frechet-covariance-domain: The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).
assumptions.ass:iid-potential-pairs: The \(n\) pairs \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) have joint law \(H^{\otimes n}\).
assumptions.ass:known-exposure: For every unit \(i\) and assignments \(w,w'\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(f_i(w)=f_i(w')\) implies \(Y_i(w)=Y_i(w')\).
assumptions.ass:product-coupling-zero: The pair \(\left(F_1\otimes F_0,\operatorname{Cov}_{F_1\otimes F_0}\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)\) belongs to \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\times\{0\}\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every rational or real-algebraic input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility, and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), the algebraic projective interval branch-and-bound procedure terminates after finitely many subdivisions and returns a locally checkable certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) such that
\[
 L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
 \qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
 \qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
The incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\) has finite real-algebraic coordinates, including when every feasible point lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  The checker verifies only CAD sign certificates, algebraic feasibility, outward objective bounds, rational norm and diameter records, chart cover, pruning inequalities, and mesh; the displayed facts about \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) are mathematical consequences.  Along every \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and meshes converge to zero.  No uniform complexity bound or semidefinite-program reduction is asserted.

defs.def:branch-bound-handle: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions, optionally tightened by interval-Hessian underestimators.  For any chart box whose feasible intersection is nonempty, repeated bisection and exact feasible-child selection produce nested closed feasible boxes with diameters tending to zero; their singleton intersection supplies the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible incumbent authorized by the certificate definition.  The procedure prunes only by exact infeasibility or by a certified box lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound, and it refines the finite quotient-chart cover and arithmetic enclosures until \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\) and \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), at which point it returns the full certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\).
defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:robust-objective: Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary maximin-gain diagnostics.  The primary robust loss and minimax value are \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).
defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:certified-input-interface: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.  Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\).  Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.
defs.def:certified-output: A corrected minimax certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) consists of a finite quotient-chart cover, an exactly feasible incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\), rational bounds \(L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon}\), outward-rounded endpoint-loss and constraint bounds for every retained box, a checkable exact-infeasibility or valid lower-bound pruning record for every discarded box, retained boxes whose union is \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\), and their maximum chart diameter \(h_{\varepsilon}\).  The exactly feasible incumbent may be represented by exact rational or real-algebraic coordinates, or by a certified inclusion-oracle name whose every requested precision terminates.  For the latter representation, exact feasibility is certified by nested closed quotient-chart boxes, each meeting \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), whose diameters tend to zero and whose intersection is the singleton \(\{B_{\varepsilon}\}\).  The checker requires \(L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon}\), \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_\varepsilon\); it never accepts deletion of a box meeting the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary without an exact infeasibility certificate or a valid objective lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound.
defs.def:argmax-correspondences: On the feasible covariance domain, where ass:product-coupling-zero and ass:frechet-covariance-domain give \(0\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\), retain \(\mathcal A_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) as the secondary maximin-gain correspondence, define the primary minimax-residual correspondence \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\), and define the ordinarily typed zero-covariance surrogate correspondence \(\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)\).

snapshot.stmt:
Along a triangular sequence satisfying ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate and ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate, let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the two endpoint matrices obtained from the unpaired empirical marginals, and put
\[
C_n=n^{-2}\left[
\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_*
+\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\right].
\]
Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot,
\[
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
=O_{L^1}\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}\right),
\qquad
C_n=O\!\left(n^{\alpha+2\beta-1}\right).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|
\le C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and the same bound without the uncontrolled term holds for \(\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)\).  Hence the exact sensitivity condition
\[
nC_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{in }L^1
\]
implies uniform first-order plug-in accuracy.  A sufficient bounded-pilot condition is
\[
\frac{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}{n^{1+\alpha+2\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]

Retain the resulting \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\) only as secondary diagnostics.  Define \(\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\}\), \(\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B)\).

The primary robust loss and minimax value are \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).

defs.def:zhao-rate-admissible-basis-class:
For a fixed \(\overline a\in[1,\infty)\), define
\[
\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}
=\left\{[B]\in\mathcal B_\kappa:
\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
This is the normalized Zhao-rate-admissible class.  The coordinate bound is imposed explicitly and is not inferred from \(\lVert b_a\rVert_2^2=n\).  Its \(\kappa\)-regularity gives \(\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge n\kappa\), so it instantiates the boundedness and nondegeneracy clauses of Zhao's Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\).

assumptions.ass:bounded-outcomes: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).
assumptions.ass:unpaired-pilot: The two arm-specific pilot samples are mutually unpaired i.i.d. draws from \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), respectively, and their joint law is independent of \(W\sim\nu\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate: There is a dependency graph \(\mathcal G_n\) for the \(2n\) coordinates of \(D\): whenever two disjoint coordinate sets have no edge between them, their indicator subvectors are independent under \(\nu\); and there are constants \(\overline d<\infty\) and \(\alpha\ge0\), independent of \(n\), such that every closed graph neighborhood has size at most \(\overline d n^{\alpha}\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate: There are constants \(\underline\pi>0\) and \(\beta\ge0\), independent of \(n\), such that \(\min_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}\pi_{i,a}\ge\underline\pi n^{-\beta}\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-coordinate-envelope: For every supplied normalized basis, \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), where \(\overline a\ge1\) is fixed along the triangular sequence.

snapshot.stmt:
Under the assumptions of lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, suppose ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence and the exact sensitivity condition hold and use the independent-pilot selectors of def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator.  Write
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}w(B),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]
Then
\[
\mathbb E_P w(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\]
and, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\),
\[
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right]
=\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)+o(n^{-1}).
\]
Thus pilot selection and feasible Horvitz--Thompson coefficient estimation each have an explicit uniform first-order bridge to the oracle endpoint loss.  In addition, if the zero-surrogate argmax is first-order stable in the following explicit sense,
\[
g_{B_n}(0)\ge\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0)-o(n^{-1})
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
w(B_n)\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1})
\]
for every deterministic sequence \(B_n\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), then
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]
The final stability clause is a property of the two ordinary-domain objective surfaces; without such a quantitative clause, ordinary outer argmax consistency alone is only \(o(1)\) and does not justify a first-order \(o(n^{-1})\) ordering.

defs.def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator:
Using only the independent unpaired pilot, choose measurable selectors
\[
\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}
\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}\widehat w(B),
\qquad
\widehat B_0
\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}\widehat g_B(0).
\]
Compactness of \(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\) and continuity of the two finite-dimensional criteria make both correspondences nonempty; a fixed lexicographic chart rule makes the selections measurable.  In the independent main experiment deploy
\[
\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}}^{\mathrm{CV}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_0}^{\mathrm{CV}}
\]
through def:observable-coefficient-map, using \(\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}\) and the ordinary inverse.  The pilot chooses the basis, while the main assignment and main potential-outcome array enter only the displayed estimator.

defs.def:observable-coefficient-map:
For observed outcomes \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(f_i(W))\), define Zhao's signed armwise Horvitz--Thompson outcome stack
\[
\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=
\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]
For \(B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\), define the ordinary-inverse Horvitz--Thompson coefficient
\[
\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)
=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
The signed stack is already inverse-probability weighted, and this coefficient applies Zhao's additional \(\Pi^{-1}\); hence
\[
\mathbb E_\nu[B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}]
=B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y.
\]
The primary feasible ordinary-inverse estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}
\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.
\]
Separately, for \(a\in\{1,0\}\), set \(\widehat1_a=n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,a}/\pi_{i,a}\) and define \(\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)=\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)/\widehat1_a\) when \(\widehat1_a>0\), and zero otherwise.  The implementation-only self-normalized variant \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV,SN}}\) is obtained by replacing \(\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)\) in the preceding display by \(\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)\).  No first-order equivalence for that variant is asserted here.  Every basis used below belongs to \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\) and therefore has an ordinary-invertible representative.

This is the maximal block-separable matrix domain on which the ordinary inverse in Zhao's Equation (8) is well defined; it is implicit in that formula and is not claimed to be a separately named domain in Zhao.  Define the quotient map \(q_Z:\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\to\mathcal B_Z\) by \(q_Z(B)=[B]\).

assumptions.ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence: The sigma-field generated by the two unpaired pilot samples is independent of the sigma-field generated jointly by \(W\) and the main potential-outcome array \(\{(Y_i(1),Y_i(0)):1\le i\le n\}\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), the ordinary-inverse loss has the exact intercept--slope form
\[
w(B)=h(0)-a_B+p_\xi(b_B).
\]
Suppose the ordinary-domain zero-covariance and minimax extrema are attained.  Then
\[
\Delta_Z=
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}\{a_B-p_\xi(b_B)\}
-\left[a^\star-\min_{B:\,a_B=a^\star}p_\xi(b_B)\right].
\]
Consequently strict ordinary-domain improvement holds if and only if \(\Delta_Z>0\), equivalently if and only if there is \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) for which
\[
\min_{C:\,a_C=a^\star}p_\xi(b_C)-p_\xi(b_B)
>a^\star-a_B.
\]
Thus some slope-penalty advantage must strictly exceed the sacrificed zero-covariance gain. \[

\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]

\[
\mathbb E_P w(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\]

\[
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)

\[

\[

\qquad

\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}\widehat g_B(0).
\]

\[

\quad\text{and}\quad
\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_0}^{\mathrm{CV}}
\]
through def:observable-coefficient-map, using \(\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}\) and the ordinary inverse.  The pilot chooses the basis, while the main assignment and main potential-outcome array enter only the displayed estimator.

defs.def:observable-coefficient-map:

\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]

\[

=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]

\[

\[

\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.

assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-coordinate-envelope: For every supplied normalized basis, \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), where \(\overline a\ge1\) is fixed along the triangular sequence.

\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
n\left|
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)

=\ell_B(c_H).
\]

defs.def:observable-coefficient-map:

\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]

\[

\[

\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right]

\]

\[
g_n^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0),
\qquad
q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B).
\]

\[

\[

\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]

\[

\[

\]

\[

\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right]
=\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)+o(n^{-1}).
\]

\[
g_n^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0),
\qquad

\]
If there are deterministic constants \(L_n\in[0,\infty)\) with \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\),
\[

\]

\[

\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]
The displayed linear error bound is a deterministic geometric property of the two ordinary-domain objective surfaces.  Without such quantitative geometry, ordinary outer argmax consistency alone is only \(o(1)\) and does not justify a first-order \(o(n^{-1})\) ordering.

defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:observable-coefficient-map:
For observed outcomes \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(f_i(W))\), define Zhao's signed armwise Horvitz--Thompson outcome stack
\[
\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=
\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]
For \(B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\), define the ordinary-inverse Horvitz--Thompson coefficient
\[
\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)
=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
The signed stack is already inverse-probability weighted, and this coefficient applies Zhao's additional \(\Pi^{-1}\); hence
\[
\mathbb E_\nu[B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}]
=B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y.
\]
The primary feasible ordinary-inverse estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}
\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.
\]
Separately, for \(a\in\{1,0\}\), set \(\widehat1_a=n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,a}/\pi_{i,a}\) and define \(\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)=\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)/\widehat1_a\) when \(\widehat1_a>0\), and zero otherwise.  The implementation-only self-normalized variant \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV,SN}}\) is obtained by replacing \(\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)\) in the preceding display by \(\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)\).  No first-order equivalence for that variant is asserted here.  Every basis used below belongs to \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\) and therefore has an ordinary-invertible representative.
defs.def:zhao-well-defined-ordinary-domain: \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z=\{B:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,\ B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\}\).  This is the maximal block-separable matrix domain on which the ordinary inverse in Zhao's Equation (8) is well defined; it is implicit in that formula and is not claimed to be a separately named domain in Zhao.  Define the quotient map \(q_Z:\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\to\mathcal B_Z\) by \(q_Z(B)=[B]\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.
defs.def:argmax-correspondences: On the feasible covariance domain, where ass:product-coupling-zero and ass:frechet-covariance-domain give \(0\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\), retain \(\mathcal A_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) as the secondary maximin-gain correspondence, define the primary minimax-residual correspondence \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\), and define the ordinarily typed zero-covariance surrogate correspondence \(\mathcal A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)\).
defs.def:ordinary-intercept-slope-image:
Let
\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), define the ordinary-domain intercept and slope
\[
a_B=g_B(0),
\qquad
b_B=-n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_BE),
\qquad g_B(c)=a_B+b_Bc,
\]
and define the endpoint drift penalty
\[
p_\xi(b)=\max\{(2/n-b)c_L,(2/n-b)c_U\}.
\]
Whenever the relevant ordinary-domain extrema are attained, put
\[
a^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}a_B,
\quad
\mathcal A_{0,Z}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}a_B,
\quad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B),
\]
\[
\Delta_Z=
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_{0,Z}}w(B_0)
-\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]

Suppose ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate, ass:zhao-first-order-rate, ass:bounded-outcomes, and ass:iid-potential-pairs hold.  Uniformly over \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), let
\[
\gamma_B^*(Y)=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y
\]
and let \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\) be the control-variate estimator using this fixed-array oracle coefficient.  There are finite constants \(K_\Delta,K_{\mathrm{cov}},K_R\), independent of \(n\), \(B\), the bounded array \(Y\), and \(H\), such that the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope
\[
R_n=K_\Delta n^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
+2K_{\mathrm{cov}}n^{(7/2)\alpha+3\beta-2},
\qquad K_R=K_\Delta+2K_{\mathrm{cov}},
\]
satisfies, for every \(n\ge3\),
\[
0\le R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
and the two uniform absolute bounds
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\0\le Y_i(a)\le1}}
\left|
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
\right|
\le R_n,
\]
\[
\sup_{\substack{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\\H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}}
\left|
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\ell_B(c_H)
\right|
\le R_n.
\]
The oracle ex ante identity is exact:
\[
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\mid Y)
=\ell_B(c_H),
\qquad
c_H=\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}.
\]
Since \(4\alpha+4\beta<1\), one has \(nR_n\to0\); hence the feasible and oracle conditional design variances differ by \(o(n^{-1})\), and the feasible ex ante variance equals \(\ell_B(c_H)+o(n^{-1})\), uniformly over the rate-admissible class.  The expectations over \(H^{\otimes n}\) are ex ante basis-performance averages, not additional randomness in the conditional design-based estimand.

Along a triangular sequence satisfying ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate and ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate, let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the two endpoint matrices obtained from the unpaired empirical marginals, and put
\[
C_n=n^{-2}\left[
\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_*
+\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\right].
\]
Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot,
\[
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
=O_{L^1}\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}\right),
\qquad
C_n=O\!\left(n^{\alpha+2\beta-1}\right).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|
\le C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Writing \(\widehat Q(0)\) for the zero-covariance moment matrix formed from the empirical marginal moments, one also has
\[
\lVert\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\]
and therefore
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|
\le 2n^{-2}\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Hence the exact sensitivity condition
\[
nC_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{in }L^1
\]
implies uniform first-order plug-in accuracy for both criteria.  A sufficient bounded-pilot condition is
\[
\frac{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}{n^{1+\alpha+2\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]

snapshot.stmt:
Under the assumptions of lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, suppose ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence and the exact sensitivity condition hold, and use the independent-pilot selectors of def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator.  Put
\[
M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
\[
d_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\qquad
e_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|.
\]
For every \(n\), almost surely under the pilot law,
\[
d_n\le C_nM_n,
\qquad
e_n\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Write
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}w(B),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]
Then the robust selector obeys the finite pilot-regret inequality
\[
0\le
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
\le2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\]
Let \(R_n\) be the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, and, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\), define
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
The feasible-estimator bridge is the finite bound
\[
|V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)|\le R_n,
\qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
\]
The exact sensitivity condition implies
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
V_s=\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)+o(n^{-1}).
\]
In addition, define
\[
g_n^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0),
\qquad
q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B).
\]
If there are deterministic \(L_n\in[0,\infty)\) with \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\),
\[
[q_n-w(B)]_+\le L_n\{g_n^\star-g_B(0)\},
\]
then the finite zero-surrogate inequality
\[
q_n-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\le4L_nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n
\]
holds, and consequently
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]

defs.def:observable-coefficient-map:
For observed outcomes \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(f_i(W))\), define Zhao's signed armwise Horvitz--Thompson outcome stack
\[
\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=
\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]

\[

=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]

\[
\mathbb E_\nu[B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}]
=B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y.
\]

\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}
\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.

snapshot.stmt:
Assume the conditions of thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer, including its deterministic linear error bound for the zero-surrogate argmax.  Suppose the attained ordinary-domain optimizer sets satisfy
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}\cup\mathcal A_{0,Z}
\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}.
\]
With \(M_n,C_n,L_n,R_n\) as in that theorem and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, define, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\),
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
Then the finite-\(n\) end-to-end lower bound is
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge
\Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n-2R_n.
\]
In particular, if explicit finite constants \(K_M,K_C,K_R\), independent of \(n\), certify
\[
\mathbb E_PM_n\le K_M\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}},
\qquad
C_n\le K_Cn^{\alpha+2\beta-1},
\qquad
R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2},
\]
then the directly checkable condition
\[
\Delta_Z>
(4L_n+2)K_CK_M
\frac{n^{\alpha+2\beta}}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}
+2K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
implies \(V_0>V_{\mathrm{mm}}\) at that finite \(n\).  If, in addition,
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\Delta_Z>0,
\]
then
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n(V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}})>0.
\]
Thus a positive first-order ordinary-domain intercept--slope gap transfers to the feasible independent-pilot estimator, with an explicit finite-\(n\) diagnostic.  The conclusion concerns ex ante expected conditional design variance; it is neither a superpopulation sampling variance nor a Wald limit law.

\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad

\]

\[
a_B=g_B(0),
\qquad
b_B=-n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_BE),
\qquad g_B(c)=a_B+b_Bc,
\]
and define the endpoint drift penalty
\[
p_\xi(b)=\max\{(2/n-b)c_L,(2/n-b)c_U\}.
\]

\[
a^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}a_B,
\quad

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose ass:exposure-positivity and ass:frechet-covariance-domain hold and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\).  For the novel Moore--Penrose completion of def:novel-pseudoinverse-completion,
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)
=\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B)
=\inf_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing}}
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B).
\]
Define the possibly empty completion equality set
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\}.
\]
Writing \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)\) for the fixed-threshold argmin, its rank-two stratum is exactly
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\cap\iota(\mathcal B_Z)
=\iota\!\left(
\bigcup_{\substack{\kappa>0:\,
\mathcal B_\kappa\ne\varnothing,\ 
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+}}
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa)\right).
\]
In particular, if the ordinary-domain infimum is attained at \(C\in\mathcal B_Z\), then \(\iota(C)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\).  Conversely, if \(\iota(C)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\), then \(C\) attains the ordinary-domain infimum and belongs to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\kappa_C)\) for some \(\kappa_C>0\) satisfying \(\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa_C}}w(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\).  The singular equality stratum is
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\setminus\iota(\mathcal B_Z)
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\le1,\ w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\}.
\]
A singular equality point need not imply attainment on \(\mathcal B_Z\).  No unconditional completion attainment, no singular equality point, and no attribution of the completion to Zhao is asserted.

defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) be the Moore--Penrose inverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) may be empty because the Moore--Penrose loss need not be lower semicontinuous across rank drops.  These are objects of the note's novel completion, not formulas or a domain attributed to Zhao.
defs.def:novel-pseudoinverse-completion: \(\mathcal B_Z^+=\{[B]_+:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where two representatives are equivalent when, separately for each arm, both columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  This is the note's novel rank-zero/rank-one/rank-two Moore--Penrose completion of \(\mathcal B_Z\); it is not Zhao's domain and attributes no singular carrier or pseudoinverse construction to Zhao.
defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).

snapshot.stmt:
There is a positive, fully explicit triangle witness whose strict separation survives every singular stratum of the novel Moore--Penrose completion.  Let \(n=3\), let
\[
G=\begin{bmatrix}0&1&1\\1&0&1\\1&1&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\nu(w)=\left(\frac13\right)^{\sum_iw_i}
       \left(\frac23\right)^{3-\sum_iw_i},
\]
and, writing \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\), define
\[
f_i(w)=
\begin{cases}
1,&w_i=1\text{ and }w_j=w_k=0,\\
0,&w_i=0\text{ and }w_j+w_k\ge1,\\
\star,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(J_3=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\top}\) and \(A=(I_3+J_3)/4\), the exact inputs are
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad c_U=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(c_L)=\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For normalized rank-two representatives \(B(x,y)\),
\[
\mathcal A_0=\{[B(x,y)]:\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,
\ \mathbf1^{\top}x=\mathbf1^{\top}y=x^{\top}y=0\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\{[B(x,y)]:\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,
\ \mathbf1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,
\ (\mathbf1^{\top}y)^2=216/55\}.
\]
They are nonempty, lie in \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), and satisfy
\[

defs.def:branch-bound-handle: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions, optionally tightened by interval-Hessian underestimators. For the triangle instance of thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate, optimization over the full maximal well-defined unquotiented ordinary-inverse domain \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\) has
\[
\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}g_{q_Z(B)}(0)=q_Z^{-1}(\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z}w(q_Z(B))=q_Z^{-1}(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}),
\]
where \(\mathcal A_0\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) are exactly the displayed normalized equality sets in that theorem.  Their values are respectively \(31/80\) and \(2613/8432\); every zero-covariance optimizer has worst-copula loss \(521/1200\), so the exact worst-loss reduction is
\[
\frac{521}{1200}-\frac{2613}{8432}=\frac{4912}{39525}>0.
\]
Thus the triangle separation holds on the entire ordinary-inverse matrix domain implicit in Zhao's Equation (8), with optimizer sets enlarged only by independent nonzero column rescaling.  The separate singular-stratum conclusions concern only the note's novel Moore--Penrose completion.

snapshot.stmt:
There is a positive, fully explicit triangle witness.  Let \(n=3\), let
\[
G=\begin{bmatrix}0&1&1\\1&0&1\\1&1&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\nu(w)=\left(\frac13\right)^{\sum_iw_i}
       \left(\frac23\right)^{3-\sum_iw_i},
\]
and, writing \(\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}\), define
\[
f_i(w)=
\begin{cases}
1,&w_i=1\text{ and }w_j=w_k=0,\\
0,&w_i=0\text{ and }w_j+w_k\ge1,\\
\star,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Take \(F_1=F_0=\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) and \(\kappa=1/8\).  With \(J_3=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\top}\) and \(A=(I_3+J_3)/4\), the exact design and endpoint inputs are
\[
\Pi=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac4{27}I_3,\frac{10}{27}I_3\right),
\qquad
\Omega=\frac1{729}
\begin{bmatrix}
108I_3-16J_3&68J_3-108I_3\\
68J_3-108I_3&162I_3+8J_3
\end{bmatrix},
\]
\[
c_L=-\frac14,
\qquad c_U=\frac14,
\qquad
Q(c_L)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&(I_3-J_3)/4\\(I_3-J_3)/4&A\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
Q(c_U)=
\begin{bmatrix}A&-A\\-A&A\end{bmatrix}.
\]
For normalized representatives \(B(x,y)=\begin{bmatrix}x&0\\0&y\end{bmatrix}\), the full optimizer correspondences are
\[
\mathcal A_0=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=\mathbf 1^{\top}y=x^{\top}y=0
\right\},
\]
and
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=
\left\{[B(x,y)]:
\lVert x\rVert_2^2=\lVert y\rVert_2^2=3,\ 
\mathbf 1^{\top}x=x^{\top}y=0,\ 
(\mathbf 1^{\top}y)^2=\frac{216}{55}
\right\}.
\]
They are nonempty, and their exact objective values satisfy
\[
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}g_B(0)=\frac{31}{80},
\qquad
w(B_0)=\frac{521}{1200}\quad(B_0\in\mathcal A_0),
\qquad
w(B_{\mathrm{mm}})=v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{2613}{8432}
\quad(B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}).
\]
Moreover every member of \(\mathcal A_0\cup\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) obeys
\[
\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)=\frac4{27}.
\]
Consequently \(\xi_0=(\nu,F_1,F_0)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak X_\kappa\), and the rational choices
\[
\delta=\frac{4912}{39525},
\qquad
\eta=\frac5{216}
\]
give the full-correspondence certificates
\[
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_0)
-\sup_{B_{\mathrm{mm}}\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)}w_{\xi_0}(B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=\delta>0
\]
and
\[
\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}(\xi_0)\cup\mathcal A_0(\xi_0)}
\left\{\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_B)-\kappa\right\}
=\eta>0.
\]

Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.
defs.def:certified-output: A corrected minimax certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) consists of a finite quotient-chart cover, an exactly feasible incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\), rational bounds \(L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon}\), outward-rounded endpoint-loss and constraint bounds for every retained box, a checkable exact-infeasibility or valid lower-bound pruning record for every discarded box, retained boxes whose union is \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\), and their maximum chart diameter \(h_{\varepsilon}\).  The exactly feasible incumbent may be represented by exact rational or real-algebraic coordinates, or by a certified inclusion-oracle name whose every requested precision terminates.  For the latter representation, exact feasibility is certified by nested closed quotient-chart boxes, each meeting \(\mathcal B_\kappa\), whose diameters tend to zero and whose intersection is the singleton \(\{B_{\varepsilon}\}\).  The checker requires \(L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon}\), \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_\varepsilon\); it never accepts deletion of a box meeting the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary without an exact infeasibility certificate or a valid objective lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound.

snapshot.stmt:
Endpoint covariances alone do not determine the minimax worst-copula residual value.  In particular, let \(n=3\), let \(W_1,W_2,W_3\) be independent Bernoulli \(1/2\) variables under \(\nu\), and set \(f_i(w)=w_i\).  With \(\kappa=1/8\) and \(\varepsilon=1/100\), the marginal pairs \((F_1,F_0)=(\delta_0,\delta_0)\) and \((F_1,F_0)=(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2),\delta_0)\) produce the same moment-incomplete tuple
\[
\Pi=\tfrac12 I_6,\qquad
\Omega=\tfrac14\begin{bmatrix}I_3&-I_3\\-I_3&I_3\end{bmatrix},
\qquad c_L=c_U=0,
\]
but their endpoint moment matrices differ and their minimax residual values are, respectively,
\[
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)=\frac1{36}.
\]
Consequently, no algorithm whose only input is \((\Pi,\Omega,c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon)\) can always return rational bounds
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le \min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon.
\]
Thus endpoint moment matrices such as \(Q(c_L)\) and \(Q(c_U)\), or equivalent marginal moments, are necessary inputs for the proposed certification problem.  This obstruction makes no claim that the corrected moment-complete branch-and-bound solver terminates at every positive tolerance.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\).  Under ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures, ass:exposure-positivity, ass:frechet-covariance-domain, and ass:product-coupling-zero,
\[
h(c)=h(0)+\frac{2c}{n}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
w(B)=h(0)+\max\left\{\frac{2c_L}{n}-g_B(c_L),\frac{2c_U}{n}-g_B(c_U)\right\}.
\]
If \(c_L<c_U\), minimization of \(w(B)\) is not algebraically equivalent to maximization of \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\): as functions of a formal endpoint-gain pair \((x_L,x_U)\), the two loss criteria are not related by a constant independent of \((x_L,x_U)\).

\[

\]

The checker verifies only CAD sign certificates, algebraic feasibility, outward objective bounds, rational norm and diameter records, chart cover, pruning inequalities, and mesh; the displayed facts about \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) are mathematical consequences.  Along every \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and meshes converge to zero.  No uniform complexity bound or semidefinite-program reduction is asserted.

Suppose ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility, ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate, ass:zhao-first-order-rate, ass:bounded-outcomes, and ass:iid-potential-pairs hold.  Uniformly over the nonempty class \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), let
\[
\gamma_B^*(Y)=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y
\]
and let \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or}}\) be the control-variate estimator using this fixed-array oracle coefficient.  There are finite constants \(K_\Delta,K_{\mathrm{cov}},K_R\), independent of \(n\), \(B\), the bounded array \(Y\), and \(H\), such that the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope
\[
R_n=K_\Delta n^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
+2K_{\mathrm{cov}}n^{(7/2)\alpha+3\beta-2},
\qquad K_R=K_\Delta+2K_{\mathrm{cov}},
\]
satisfies, for every \(n\ge3\),
\[

\[

defs.def:observable-coefficient-map:
For observed outcomes \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(f_i(W))\), define Zhao's signed armwise Horvitz--Thompson outcome stack
\[

\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]

\[

\]

\[

=B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y.

\[

=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}

assumptions.ass:bounded-outcomes: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).

assumptions.ass:iid-potential-pairs: The \(n\) pairs \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) have joint law \(H^{\otimes n}\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate: There is a dependency graph \(\mathcal G_n\) for the \(2n\) coordinates of \(D\): whenever two disjoint coordinate sets have no edge between them, their indicator subvectors are independent under \(\nu\); and there are constants \(\overline d<\infty\) and \(\alpha\ge0\), independent of \(n\), such that every closed graph neighborhood has size at most \(\overline d n^{\alpha}\).

assumptions.ass:frechet-covariance-domain: The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).
assumptions.ass:product-coupling-zero: The pair \(\left(F_1\otimes F_0,\operatorname{Cov}_{F_1\otimes F_0}\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\}\right)\) belongs to \(\Gamma(F_1,F_0)\times\{0\}\).

\[
C_n=n^{-2}\left[
\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_*
+\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\right].
\]
Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot,
\[
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
=O_{L^1}\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}\right),
\qquad
C_n=O\!\left(n^{\alpha+2\beta-1}\right).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|
\le C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Writing \(\widehat Q(0)\) for the zero-covariance moment matrix formed from the empirical marginal moments, one also has
\[
\lVert\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\]
and therefore
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|
\le 2n^{-2}\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2C_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Hence the exact sensitivity condition
\[
nC_n\max_e\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{in }L^1
\]
implies uniform first-order plug-in accuracy for both criteria.  A sufficient bounded-pilot condition is
\[
\frac{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}{n^{1+\alpha+2\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]

Suppose ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility holds.  Under the assumptions of lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, suppose ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence and the exact sensitivity condition hold, and use the independent-pilot selectors of def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator.  Put
\[
M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
\[
d_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\qquad
e_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|.
\]
For every \(n\), almost surely under the pilot law,
\[
d_n\le C_nM_n,
\qquad e_n\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Write
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}w(B),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]
Then the robust selector obeys the finite pilot-regret inequality
\[
0\le
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
\le2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\]
Let \(R_n\) be the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, and, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\), define
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
The feasible-estimator bridge is the finite bound
\[
|V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)|\le R_n,
\qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
\]
The exact sensitivity condition implies
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
V_s=\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)+o(n^{-1}).
\]
In addition, define
\[
g_n^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0),
\qquad
q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B).
\]
If there are deterministic \(L_n\in[0,\infty)\) with \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\),
\[
[q_n-w(B)]_+\le L_n\{g_n^\star-g_B(0)\},
\]
then the finite zero-surrogate inequality
\[
q_n-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\le4L_nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n
\]
holds, and consequently
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]
The linear error bound is a deterministic geometric property of the two ordinary-domain objective surfaces.  Without it, ordinary outer argmax consistency alone is only \(o(1)\) and does not justify a first-order \(o(n^{-1})\) ordering.

snapshot.stmt:
For every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), the ordinary-inverse loss has the exact intercept--slope form
\[
w(B)=h(0)-a_B+p_\xi(b_B).
\]
Suppose the ordinary-domain zero-covariance and minimax extrema are attained.  Then
\[
\Delta_Z=
\max_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}\{a_B-p_\xi(b_B)\}
-\left[a^\star-\inf_{B:\,a_B=a^\star}p_\xi(b_B)\right].
\]
Consequently strict ordinary-domain improvement holds if and only if \(\Delta_Z>0\), equivalently if and only if there is \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) for which
\[
\inf_{C:\,a_C=a^\star}p_\xi(b_C)-p_\xi(b_B)
>a^\star-a_B.
\]
Thus some slope-penalty advantage must strictly exceed the sacrificed zero-covariance gain.  Through \(q_Z\), all displayed values are unchanged on \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\), and every attained optimizer correspondence there is exactly the inverse image of its projective correspondence.  No universal strictness, minimax interchange, singular completion, or semidefinite reduction is asserted.

defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:ordinary-intercept-slope-image:
Let
\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), define the ordinary-domain intercept and slope
\[
a_B=g_B(0),
\qquad
b_B=-n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_BE),
\qquad g_B(c)=a_B+b_Bc,
\]
and define the endpoint drift penalty
\[
p_\xi(b)=\max\{(2/n-b)c_L,(2/n-b)c_U\}.
\]
Whenever the relevant ordinary-domain extrema are attained, put
\[
a^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}a_B,
\quad
\mathcal A_{0,Z}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}a_B,
\quad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B),
\]
\[
\Delta_Z=
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_{0,Z}}w(B_0)
-\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
These objects use only the positive-definite ordinary-inverse domain; no singular or Moore--Penrose class is included.

defs.def:zhao-well-defined-ordinary-domain: \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z=\{B:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,\ B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\}\).  This is the maximal block-separable matrix domain on which the ordinary inverse in Zhao's Equation (8) is well defined; it is implicit in that formula and is not claimed to be a separately named domain in Zhao.  Define the quotient map \(q_Z:\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\to\mathcal B_Z\) by \(q_Z(B)=[B]\).

snapshot.stmt:
Assume ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility and the conditions of thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer, including its deterministic linear error bound for the zero-surrogate argmax.  Suppose the attained ordinary-domain optimizer sets satisfy
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}\cup\mathcal A_{0,Z}
\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}.
\]
With \(M_n,C_n,L_n,R_n\) as in that theorem and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, define, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\),
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
Then the finite-\(n\) end-to-end lower bound is
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge
\Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n-2R_n.
\]
In particular, if explicit finite constants \(K_M,K_C,K_R\), independent of \(n\), certify
\[
\mathbb E_PM_n\le K_M\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}},
\qquad
C_n\le K_Cn^{\alpha+2\beta-1},
\qquad
R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2},
\]
then the directly checkable condition
\[
\Delta_Z>
(4L_n+2)K_CK_M
\frac{n^{\alpha+2\beta}}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}
+2K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
implies \(V_0>V_{\mathrm{mm}}\) at that finite \(n\).  If, in addition,
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\Delta_Z>0,
\]
then
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n(V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}})>0.
\]
Thus a positive first-order ordinary-domain intercept--slope gap transfers to the feasible independent-pilot estimator, with an explicit finite-\(n\) diagnostic.  The conclusion concerns ex ante expected conditional design variance; it is neither a superpopulation sampling variance nor a Wald limit law.

defs.def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator:
Under ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility and using only the independent unpaired pilot, define
\[
\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}
\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}\widehat w(B),
\qquad
\widehat B_0
\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}\widehat g_B(0)
\]
by the fixed lexicographic quotient-chart tie-breaking rule.  In the independent main experiment deploy
\[
\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}}^{\mathrm{CV}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_0}^{\mathrm{CV}}
\]
through def:observable-coefficient-map, using \(\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}\) and the ordinary inverse.  The pilot chooses the basis, while the main assignment and main potential-outcome array enter only the displayed estimator.  The existence and measurability of these selectors are derived from the named nonemptiness condition, compactness, continuity, and measurable dependence in thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer; no out-of-class fallback is part of the construction.
defs.def:zhao-rate-admissible-basis-class:
For a fixed \(\overline a\in[1,\infty)\), define
\[
\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}
=\left\{[B]\in\mathcal B_\kappa:
\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
This is the normalized Zhao-rate-admissible class.  The coordinate bound is imposed explicitly and is not inferred from \(\lVert b_a\rVert_2^2=n\).  Its \(\kappa\)-regularity gives \(\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge n\kappa\), so it instantiates the boundedness and nondegeneracy clauses of Zhao's Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\).
defs.def:pilot-plugin: Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\); substitute them into \(Q(c_L),Q(c_U)\), \(h(c)\), \(g_B(c)\), and \(\ell_B(c)\).  Retain the resulting \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat r(B)\) only as secondary diagnostics. defs.def:observable-coefficient-map:
For observed outcomes \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(f_i(W))\), define Zhao's signed armwise Horvitz--Thompson outcome stack
\[
\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=
\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]
For \(B\in\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\), define the ordinary-inverse Horvitz--Thompson coefficient
\[
\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)
=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
The signed stack is already inverse-probability weighted, and this coefficient applies Zhao's additional \(\Pi^{-1}\); hence
\[
\mathbb E_\nu[B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}]
=B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Y.
\]
The primary feasible ordinary-inverse estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}
\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.
\]
Separately, for \(a\in\{1,0\}\), set \(\widehat1_a=n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,a}/\pi_{i,a}\) and define \(\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)=\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)/\widehat1_a\) when \(\widehat1_a>0\), and zero otherwise. No first-order equivalence for that variant is asserted here.  Every basis used below belongs to \(\mathcal B_\kappa\subseteq\mathcal B_Z\) and therefore has an ordinary-invertible representative.

Define \(\iota:\mathcal B_Z\to\mathcal B_Z^+\) by \(\iota([B])=[B]_+\).  This map is a well-defined bijection from \(\mathcal B_Z\) onto
\[

\]
For every \([B]\in\mathcal B_Z\) and every \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\),
\[
 g_{\iota(B)}^+(c)=g_B(c),
 \qquad \ell_{\iota(B)}^+(c)=\ell_B(c),

\]

defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:

defs.def:branch-bound-handle: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions, optionally tightened by interval-Hessian underestimators.  For any chart box whose feasible intersection is nonempty, repeated bisection and exact feasible-child selection produce nested closed feasible boxes with diameters tending to zero; their singleton intersection supplies the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible incumbent authorized by the certificate definition. defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) be the Moore--Penrose inverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) may be empty because the Moore--Penrose loss need not be lower semicontinuous across rank drops.  These are objects of the note's novel completion, not formulas or a domain attributed to Zhao.

\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}\le w(B_{\varepsilon})\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad
U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal C_{\varepsilon}.
\]
Here \(B_{\varepsilon}\in\mathcal B_\kappa\) is represented exactly, including when the feasible set has no relative interior and lies on \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)=\kappa\).  A chart box meeting that equality boundary is never discarded as infeasible; it may be discarded only when its certified objective lower bound exceeds the incumbent upper bound.  Consequently, along any sequence \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), the certified value gaps and retained-box mesh diameters converge to zero.  This is a finite, instance-dependent termination result; it asserts neither a uniform complexity bound nor a semidefinite-program reduction.

defs.def:branch-bound-handle: Given the moment-complete \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the projective interval branch-and-bound procedure covers each normalized projective factor by the finite pivot-coordinate charts \(\{|b_j|\ge n^{-1/2}\}\), bisects retained boxes, handles the sphere equations and the exact \(\kappa\)-boundary through the feasibility interface, and bounds both endpoint residual losses and every constraint by outward-rounded interval extensions, optionally tightened by interval-Hessian underestimators.  For any chart box whose feasible intersection is nonempty, repeated bisection and exact feasible-child selection produce nested closed feasible boxes with diameters tending to zero; their singleton intersection supplies the certified inclusion-oracle name of an exactly feasible incumbent authorized by the certificate definition.  The procedure prunes only by exact infeasibility or by a certified box lower bound exceeding the incumbent upper bound, and it refines the finite quotient-chart cover and arithmetic enclosures until \(U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\) and \(h_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon\), at which point it returns the full certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\).

defs.def:certified-output: A corrected minimax certificate \(\mathscr K_{\varepsilon}\) consists of a finite quotient-chart cover, an exactly feasible incumbent \(B_{\varepsilon}\), rational bounds \(L_{\varepsilon},U_{\varepsilon}\), outward-rounded endpoint-loss and constraint bounds for every retained box, a checkable exact-infeasibility or valid lower-bound pruning record for every discarded box, retained boxes whose union is \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\), and their maximum chart diameter \(h_{\varepsilon}\).
