defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) be the Moore--Penrose inverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) may be empty because the Moore--Penrose loss need not be lower semicontinuous across rank drops.  These are objects of the note's novel completion, not formulas or a domain attributed to Zhao.
defs.def:novel-pseudoinverse-completion: \(\mathcal B_Z^+=\{[B]_+:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where two representatives are equivalent when, separately for each arm, both columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  This is the note's novel rank-zero/rank-one/rank-two Moore--Penrose completion of \(\mathcal B_Z\); it is not Zhao's domain and attributes no singular carrier or pseudoinverse construction to Zhao.

snapshot.stmt:
For every rational signed pivot-chart box, intersection with the normalized feasible set \(\mathcal B_\kappa\) is an existential semialgebraic question.  More explicitly, sphere feasibility, chart and box restrictions, and \(S_B-n\kappa I_2\succeq0\) are finitely many polynomial equalities and weak inequalities with rational or real-algebraic coefficients; for
\[
 S_B-n\kappa I_2=\begin{bmatrix}u&v\\v&z\end{bmatrix},
\]
the matrix inequality is exactly \(u\ge0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(uz-v^2\ge0\).  Cylindrical algebraic decomposition therefore terminates with either an exact real-algebraic feasible sample or a finite infeasibility certificate, including when feasibility occurs only on the equality boundary.

defs.def:certified-input-interface: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.  Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\).  Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.

The primary robust loss and minimax value are \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).

snapshot.stmt: Under ass:mutually-exclusive-exposures and ass:exposure-positivity, every \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) has affine functions \(c\mapsto g_B(c)\) and \(c\mapsto\ell_B(c)\) on the imported feasible domain \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\). Consequently, \(\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}\ell_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\), with both extrema attained. The product coupling gives \(c_L\le0\le c_U\), so \(g_B(0)\) is an ordinarily typed feasible-covariance gain. If \(c_L<0<c_U\), \(g_B(0)=\inf_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}g_B(\operatorname{Cov}_H\{Y_i(1),Y_i(0)\})\) if and only if the affine slope of \(g_B\) is zero.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility hold.  Under the assumptions of lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, suppose ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence and the exact sensitivity condition hold, and use the independent-pilot selectors of def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator.  Put
\[
M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
\[
d_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\qquad
e_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|.
\]
For every \(n\), almost surely under the pilot law,
\[
d_n\le C_nM_n,
\qquad e_n\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Write
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}w(B),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]
Then the robust selector obeys the finite pilot-regret inequality
\[
0\le
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
\le2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\]
Let \(R_n\) be the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, and, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\), define
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
The feasible-estimator bridge is the finite bound
\[
|V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)|\le R_n,
\qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
\]
The exact sensitivity condition implies
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
V_s=\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)+o(n^{-1}).
\]
In addition, define
\[
g_n^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0),
\qquad
q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B).
\]
If there are deterministic \(L_n\in[0,\infty)\) with \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\),
\[
[q_n-w(B)]_+\le L_n\{g_n^\star-g_B(0)\},
\]
then the finite zero-surrogate inequality
\[
q_n-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\le4L_nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n
\]
holds, and consequently
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]
The linear error bound is a deterministic geometric property of the two ordinary-domain objective surfaces.  Without it, ordinary outer argmax consistency alone is only \(o(1)\) and does not justify a first-order \(o(n^{-1})\) ordering.  These selectors and limits are secondary regular rank-two deployment results.  No primitive condition in this theorem proves existence of uniformly bounded \(L_n\); the zero-surrogate first-order conclusion is conditional on the displayed global linear error bound.

defs.def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator:
Under ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility, and using only the independent unpaired pilot, define the regular rank-two selectors
\[
\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}
\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}\widehat w(B),
\qquad
\widehat B_0
\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}\widehat g_B(0)
\]
by the fixed lexicographic quotient-chart tie-breaking rule.  In the independent main experiment deploy \(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}}^{\mathrm{CV}}\) and \(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_0}^{\mathrm{CV}}\) through def:observable-coefficient-map.  On this class Zhao's published pseudoinverse equals the ordinary inverse.  The pilot chooses the basis, while the main assignment and main potential-outcome array enter only the displayed estimator.  The existence and measurability of these selectors are derived in thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer; no out-of-class fallback is part of the construction.  This construction is the regular deployable restriction, not the primary full-class epsilon-minimizer rule.
defs.def:zhao-rate-admissible-basis-class:
For a fixed \(\overline a\in[1,\infty)\), define
\[
\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}
=\left\{[B]\in\mathcal B_\kappa:
\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
This is the normalized Zhao-rate-admissible class.  The coordinate bound is imposed explicitly and is not inferred from \(\lVert b_a\rVert_2^2=n\).  Its \(\kappa\)-regularity gives \(\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge n\kappa\), so it instantiates the boundedness and nondegeneracy clauses of Zhao's Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\).
defs.def:pilot-plugin:
Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\), and let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the resulting endpoint matrices.  On the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, define the distinct full-class empirical objective
\[
\widehat w_m^+(B)=
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\}\widehat Q_e
\right].
\]
For every positive deterministic or pilot-measurable tolerance \(\varepsilon_m\), define \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+\) by a fixed rank-pattern and signed-chart lexicographic rule among bases satisfying
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
\le
\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m.
\]
Such a basis exists for every \(\varepsilon_m>0\) by the defining property of the infimum; no exact full-class argmin is assumed.  On the compact fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, separately retain
\[
\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\},
\quad
\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\quad
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\]
and retain \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) only as secondary diagnostics.  The full-class epsilon selector and the regular rank-two exact argmin are not conflated.
defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) denote Zhao's published spectral pseudoinverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and the zero-covariance argmax set may be empty because the rank-stratified pseudoinverse criteria need not attain their extrema across rank changes.  These are criteria induced by Zhao's published unquotiented carrier and expressed on the note's projective quotient; no attainment is built into the definition.
defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\qquad b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  Thus \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, not a projective class named by Zhao.  Its rank-two positive-definite stratum is the image of \(\mathcal B_Z\) under \(\iota\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.
defs.def:robust-objective: The primary robust criterion on the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain is \(w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\}\), with value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\).  On the deployable fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, retain \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).  Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary regular-class maximin-gain diagnostics.
defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:observable-coefficient-map:
Define the realized outcome \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(W)\) and Zhao's signed armwise Horvitz--Thompson stack
\[
\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=
\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]
For a representative of \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), define Zhao's published pseudoinverse coefficient
\[
\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)
=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
\]
and the observable control-variate estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}
\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), \((B^{\top}\Omega B)^+=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}\), so these maps reduce to the ordinary-inverse rank-two formulas used by the finite-rate results.  Separately define \(\widehat1_a=n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,a}/\pi_{i,a}\), \(\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)=\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)/\widehat1_a\) when \(\widehat1_a>0\) and zero otherwise, and obtain \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV,SN}}\) by substitution.  No first-order equivalence for the self-normalized variant is asserted.  The expectation identity needed for the oracle comparison is not built into this definition; it is derived from ass:known-exposure in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence.

assumptions.ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility: There exist \(b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\) such that, for \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\), \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n\), \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), and \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\).
assumptions.ass:frechet-covariance-domain: The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).
assumptions.ass:known-exposure: For every unit \(i\) and assignments \(w,w'\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(f_i(w)=f_i(w')\) implies \(Y_i(w)=Y_i(w')\).
assumptions.ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence: The sigma-field generated by the two unpaired pilot samples is independent of the sigma-field generated jointly by \(W\) and the main potential-outcome array \(\{(Y_i(1),Y_i(0)):1\le i\le n\}\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-coordinate-envelope: For every supplied normalized basis, \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), where \(\overline a\ge1\) is fixed along the triangular sequence.

snapshot.stmt:
Assume ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility and the conditions of thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer, including its deterministic linear error bound for the zero-surrogate argmax.  Suppose the attained ordinary-domain optimizer sets satisfy
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}\cup\mathcal A_{0,Z}
\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}.
\]
With \(M_n,C_n,L_n,R_n\) as in that theorem and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, define, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\),
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
Then the finite-\(n\) end-to-end lower bound is
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge
\Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n-2R_n.
\]
In particular, if explicit finite constants \(K_M,K_C,K_R\), independent of \(n\), certify
\[
\mathbb E_PM_n\le K_M\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}},
\qquad
C_n\le K_Cn^{\alpha+2\beta-1},
\qquad
R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2},
\]
then the directly checkable condition
\[
\Delta_Z>
(4L_n+2)K_CK_M
\frac{n^{\alpha+2\beta}}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}
+2K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
implies \(V_0>V_{\mathrm{mm}}\) at that finite \(n\).  If, in addition,
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\Delta_Z>0,
\]
then
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n(V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}})>0.
\]
Thus a positive first-order ordinary-domain intercept--slope gap transfers to the feasible independent-pilot estimator, with an explicit finite-\(n\) diagnostic.  The conclusion concerns ex ante expected conditional design variance; it is neither a superpopulation sampling variance nor a Wald limit law.  Neither the optimizer-containment condition nor a primitive theorem yielding uniformly bounded \(L_n\) is proved here; both are separate checkable hypotheses.  The proposition concerns the positive-definite rank-two restriction only.

=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
\]

\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}

Fix \(G,\nu,(f_i)_{i=1}^n\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity.  Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot, let \(\widehat w_m^+(B)\) and, for \(\varepsilon_m>0\), \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+\) be the distinct full-class empirical objective and selector in def:pilot-plugin, and put
\[
d_m^+=\sup_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}|\widehat w_m^+(B)-w^+(B)|.
\]
As \(m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty\), \(d_m^+\to0\) almost surely and
\[
\left|\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\right|
\le d_m^+\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
For every positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\),
\[
w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++2d_m^++\varepsilon_m.
\]
Consequently, if \(\varepsilon_m\to0\) almost surely, then
\[
w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\longrightarrow0
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
The domain is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain.  No exact selector at zero tolerance, cross-rank outer-argmin convergence, or point convergence is asserted without attainment and rank-separation conditions.

defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[

\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero. defs.def:pilot-plugin:
Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\), and let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the resulting endpoint matrices. \[

\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}

\right].

\le

\]

 w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+

The uniform plug-in inequalities are
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|
\le C_nM_n,
\]
and, writing \(\widehat Q(0)\) for the zero-covariance moment matrix formed from the empirical marginal moments,
\[
\lVert\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2M_n,
\]
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|
\le2n^{-2}\sup_B\lVert A_B\rVert_*M_n
\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Hence the exact downstream premise
\[
nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\longrightarrow0
\]
implies first-order plug-in accuracy in the explicit sense that the pilot expectations of both displayed uniform criterion errors are \(o(n^{-1})\).  The condition
\[
\frac{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}{n^{1+\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty
\]
is sufficient.  Neither known exposure nor a dependency-neighborhood condition is used in this pilot-only matrix calculation.

defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:pilot-plugin:
Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\), and let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the resulting endpoint matrices.  On the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, define the distinct full-class empirical objective
\[
\widehat w_m^+(B)=
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\}\widehat Q_e
\right].
\]
For every positive deterministic or pilot-measurable tolerance \(\varepsilon_m\), define \(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+\) by a fixed rank-pattern and signed-chart lexicographic rule among bases satisfying
\[
\widehat w_m^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)
\le
\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m.
\]
Such a basis exists for every \(\varepsilon_m>0\) by the defining property of the infimum; no exact full-class argmin is assumed.  On the compact fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, separately retain
\[
\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\},
\quad
\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\quad
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\]
and retain \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) only as secondary diagnostics.  The full-class epsilon selector and the regular rank-two exact argmin are not conflated.
defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) denote Zhao's published spectral pseudoinverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and the zero-covariance argmax set may be empty because the rank-stratified pseudoinverse criteria need not attain their extrema across rank changes.  These are criteria induced by Zhao's published unquotiented carrier and expressed on the note's projective quotient; no attainment is built into the definition.
defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\qquad b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  Thus \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, not a projective class named by Zhao.  Its rank-two positive-definite stratum is the image of \(\mathcal B_Z\) under \(\iota\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.
defs.def:robust-objective: The primary robust criterion on the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain is \(w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\}\), with value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\).  On the deployable fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, retain \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).  Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary regular-class maximin-gain diagnostics.
defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:zhao-rate-admissible-basis-class:
For a fixed \(\overline a\in[1,\infty)\), define
\[
\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}
=\left\{[B]\in\mathcal B_\kappa:
\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
This is the normalized Zhao-rate-admissible class.  The coordinate bound is imposed explicitly and is not inferred from \(\lVert b_a\rVert_2^2=n\).  Its \(\kappa\)-regularity gives \(\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge n\kappa\), so it instantiates the boundedness and nondegeneracy clauses of Zhao's Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\).

assumptions.ass:bounded-outcomes: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).
assumptions.ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility: There exist \(b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\) such that, for \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\), \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n\), \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), and \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\).
assumptions.ass:unpaired-pilot: The two arm-specific pilot samples are mutually unpaired i.i.d. draws from \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), respectively, and their joint law is independent of \(W\sim\nu\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate: There are constants \(\underline\pi>0\) and \(\beta\ge0\), independent of \(n\), such that \(\min_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}\pi_{i,a}\ge\underline\pi n^{-\beta}\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-coordinate-envelope: For every supplied normalized basis, \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), where \(\overline a\ge1\) is fixed along the triangular sequence.

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility hold.  Under the assumptions of lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, suppose ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence holds, and use the independent-pilot selectors of def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator.  Put
\[
M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
where \(C_n\) is exactly the deterministic sensitivity coefficient defined in lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate, and assume along the triangular sequence that
\[
nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\longrightarrow0.
\]
Put also
\[
d_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\qquad
e_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|.
\]
For every \(n\), almost surely under the pilot law,
\[
d_n\le C_nM_n,
\qquad e_n\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Write
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}w(B),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]
Then the robust selector obeys the finite pilot-regret inequality
\[
0\le
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
\le2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\]
Let \(R_n\) be the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, and, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\), define
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
The feasible-estimator bridge is the finite bound
\[
|V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)|\le R_n,
\qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
\]
Under \(nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\to0\),
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
V_s=\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)+o(n^{-1}).
\]
In addition, define
\[
g_n^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0),
\qquad
q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B).
\]
If there are deterministic \(L_n\in[0,\infty)\) with \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\),
\[
[q_n-w(B)]_+\le L_n\{g_n^\star-g_B(0)\},
\]
then the finite zero-surrogate inequality
\[
q_n-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\le4L_nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n
\]
holds, and consequently
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]
The linear error bound is a deterministic geometric property of the two ordinary-domain objective surfaces.  Without it, ordinary outer argmax consistency alone is only \(o(1)\) and does not justify a first-order \(o(n^{-1})\) ordering.  These selectors and limits are secondary regular rank-two deployment results.  No primitive condition in this theorem proves existence of uniformly bounded \(L_n\); the zero-surrogate first-order conclusion is conditional on the displayed global linear error bound.

\[

\qquad

defs.def:observable-coefficient-map:
Define the realized outcome \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(W)\) and Zhao's signed armwise Horvitz--Thompson stack
\[
\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=
\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]
For a representative of \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), define Zhao's published pseudoinverse coefficient
\[
\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)
=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
\]
and the observable control-variate estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}
\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), \((B^{\top}\Omega B)^+=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}\), so these maps reduce to the ordinary-inverse rank-two formulas used by the finite-rate results.  Separately define \(\widehat1_a=n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,a}/\pi_{i,a}\), \(\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)=\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)/\widehat1_a\) when \(\widehat1_a>0\) and zero otherwise, and obtain \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV,SN}}\) by substitution.  No first-order equivalence for the self-normalized variant is asserted.  The expectation identity needed for the oracle comparison is not built into this definition; it is derived from ass:known-exposure in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence.

assumptions.ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility: There exist \(b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\) such that, for \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\), \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n\), \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), and \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\).
assumptions.ass:frechet-covariance-domain: The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).
assumptions.ass:known-exposure: For every unit \(i\) and assignments \(w,w'\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(f_i(w)=f_i(w')\) implies \(Y_i(w)=Y_i(w')\).
assumptions.ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence: The sigma-field generated by the two unpaired pilot samples is independent of the sigma-field generated jointly by \(W\) and the main potential-outcome array \(\{(Y_i(1),Y_i(0)):1\le i\le n\}\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-coordinate-envelope: For every supplied normalized basis, \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), where \(\overline a\ge1\) is fixed along the triangular sequence.

Under ass:bounded-outcomes, ass:unpaired-pilot, and ass:exposure-positivity, suppose \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\), and define
\[
 M_m=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
 \qquad
 d_m^+=\sup_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}
 |\widehat w_m^+(B)-w^+(B)|,
\]
and let \(\pi_{\min,n}=\min_{i,a}\pi_{i,a}>0\).  For every rank zero, one, or two class \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\),
\[
 0\preceq A_B^+\preceq A_{\mathrm{HT}},
 \qquad
 A_B^+=\Pi^{-1}\Omega^{1/2}P_B\Omega^{1/2}\Pi^{-1},
 \qquad
 A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1},
\]
and
\[
 d_m^+\le 4\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}n^{-1}M_m.
\]
Along a triangular sequence satisfying ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate and \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\) at every \(n\), this yields
\[
 d_m^+\le4\underline\pi^{-1}n^{\beta-1}M_m
\tag{A}
\]
and, for every positive deterministic or pilot-measurable \(\varepsilon_m\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
 w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
 \right]
 \le
 8\underline\pi^{-1}n^{\beta-1}\mathbb E_P[M_m]
 +\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_m].
\tag{B}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}{n^{1+\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad n\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_m]\longrightarrow0
\]
imply
\[
 n\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
 \right]\longrightarrow0.
\]
This is a full-carrier basis-objective regret result on the note's quotient of Zhao's all-rank pseudoinverse domain.  It is not a feasible-estimator variance bridge for a selected singular-rank basis.

Along a triangular sequence satisfying ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility and ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate, let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the two endpoint matrices obtained from the unpaired empirical marginals, put \(M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\), and define
\[
C_n=n^{-2}\left[
\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\rVert_*
+\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}
\left\lVert\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\rVert_*
\right].
\]
Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot,
\[
M_n=O_{L^1}\!\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}\right),
\qquad
C_n\le4\underline\pi^{-1}n^{\beta-1}.
\]
More precisely, with
\[
A_{\mathrm{HT}}=\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1},
\qquad
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1},
\]
one has
\[
0\preceq A_B\preceq A_{\mathrm{HT}},
\qquad
\lVert A_B\rVert_*
\le\operatorname{tr}(A_{\mathrm{HT}})
=\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_{a\in\{1,0\}}\frac{1-\pi_{i,a}}{\pi_{i,a}}
\le2\underline\pi^{-1}n^{1+\beta}.
\]
The uniform plug-in inequalities are
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|
\le C_nM_n,
\]
and, writing \(\widehat Q(0)\) for the zero-covariance moment matrix formed from the empirical marginal moments,
\[
\lVert\widehat Q(0)-Q(0)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2M_n,
\]
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|
\le2n^{-2}\sup_B\lVert A_B\rVert_*M_n
\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Hence the exact downstream premise
\[
nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\longrightarrow0
\]
implies first-order plug-in accuracy in the explicit sense that the pilot expectations of both displayed uniform criterion errors are \(o(n^{-1})\).  The condition
\[
\frac{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}{n^{1+\beta}}\longrightarrow\infty
\]
is sufficient.  Neither known exposure nor a dependency-neighborhood condition is used in this pilot-only matrix calculation.

defs.def:pilot-plugin:

\[
\widehat w_m^+(B)=
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\}\widehat Q_e
\right].
\]

\[

 \qquad

\]

\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),

defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:zhao-rate-admissible-basis-class:
For a fixed \(\overline a\in[1,\infty)\), define
\[

=\left\{[B]\in\mathcal B_\kappa:
\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\right\}.
\]

snapshot.stmt:
Suppose ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility hold.  Under the assumptions of lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, suppose ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence holds, and use the independent-pilot selectors of def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator.  Put
\[
M_n=\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}\lVert\widehat Q_e-Q(c_e)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
where \(C_n\) is exactly the deterministic sensitivity coefficient defined in lem:uniform-pilot-endpoint-matrix-rate, and assume along the triangular sequence that
\[
nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\longrightarrow0.
\]
Put also
\[
d_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\qquad
e_n=\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|.
\]
For every \(n\), almost surely under the pilot law,
\[
d_n\le C_nM_n,
\qquad e_n\le2C_nM_n.
\]
Write
\[
v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}w(B),
\qquad
\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0).
\]
Then the robust selector obeys the finite pilot-regret inequality
\[
0\le
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})-v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}
\le2C_n\mathbb E_PM_n.
\]
Let \(R_n\) be the deterministic finite-\(n\) envelope in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, and, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\), define
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
The feasible-estimator bridge is the finite bound
\[
|V_s-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)|\le R_n,
\qquad s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}.
\]
Under \(nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\to0\),
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})
=v_{\mathrm{mm},\overline a}+o(n^{-1}),
\qquad
V_s=\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_s)+o(n^{-1}).
\]
In addition, define
\[
g_n^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}g_B(0),
\qquad
q_n=\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B).
\]
If there are deterministic \(L_n\in[0,\infty)\) with \(\sup_nL_n<\infty\) such that, for every \(B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\),
\[
[q_n-w(B)]_+\le L_n\{g_n^\star-g_B(0)\},
\]
then the finite zero-surrogate inequality
\[
q_n-\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\le4L_nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n
\]
holds, and consequently
\[
\mathbb E_Pw(\widehat B_0)
\ge\inf_{B\in\mathcal A_{0,\overline a}}w(B)-o(n^{-1}).
\]
The linear error bound is a deterministic geometric property of the two ordinary-domain objective surfaces.  Without it, ordinary outer argmax consistency alone is only \(o(1)\) and does not justify a first-order \(o(n^{-1})\) ordering.  These selectors and limits are secondary regular rank-two deployment results.  No primitive condition in this theorem proves existence of uniformly bounded \(L_n\); the zero-surrogate first-order conclusion is conditional on the displayed global linear error bound.

defs.def:observable-coefficient-map:
Define the realized outcome \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(W)\) and Zhao's signed armwise Horvitz--Thompson stack
\[
\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=
\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]
For a representative of \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), define Zhao's published pseudoinverse coefficient
\[
\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)
=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
\]
and the observable control-variate estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}
\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.
\]

assumptions.ass:frechet-covariance-domain: The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).
assumptions.ass:known-exposure: For every unit \(i\) and assignments \(w,w'\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(f_i(w)=f_i(w')\) implies \(Y_i(w)=Y_i(w')\).
assumptions.ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence: The sigma-field generated by the two unpaired pilot samples is independent of the sigma-field generated jointly by \(W\) and the main potential-outcome array \(\{(Y_i(1),Y_i(0)):1\le i\le n\}\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-coordinate-envelope: For every supplied normalized basis, \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), where \(\overline a\ge1\) is fixed along the triangular sequence.

snapshot.stmt:
Assume ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility and the conditions of thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer, including its exact hypothesis \(nC_n\mathbb E_PM_n\to0\) and its deterministic linear error bound for the zero-surrogate argmax.  Suppose the attained ordinary-domain optimizer sets satisfy
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}\cup\mathcal A_{0,Z}
\subseteq\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}.
\]
With \(M_n,C_n,L_n,R_n\) as in that theorem and lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence, define, for \(s\in\{\mathrm{mm},0\}\),
\[
V_s=
\mathbb E_P\left[
\sup_{H\in\Gamma(F_1,F_0)}
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu
(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_s}^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid\widehat B_s,Y)
\right].
\]
Then the finite-\(n\) end-to-end lower bound is
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge
\Delta_Z-(4L_n+2)C_n\mathbb E_PM_n-2R_n.
\]
In particular, if explicit finite constants \(K_M,K_C,K_R\), independent of \(n\), certify
\[
\mathbb E_PM_n\le K_M\frac{n}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}},
\qquad
C_n\le K_Cn^{\beta-1},
\qquad
R_n\le K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2},
\]
then the directly checkable condition
\[
\Delta_Z>
(4L_n+2)K_CK_M
\frac{n^{\beta}}{\sqrt{m_1\wedge m_0}}
+2K_Rn^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
\]
implies \(V_0>V_{\mathrm{mm}}\) at that finite \(n\).  If, in addition,
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\Delta_Z>0,
\]
then
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n(V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}})>0.
\]
Thus a positive first-order ordinary-domain intercept--slope gap transfers to the feasible independent-pilot estimator, with an explicit finite-\(n\) diagnostic and the sharpened pilot term.  The conclusion concerns ex ante expected conditional design variance; it is neither a superpopulation sampling variance nor a Wald limit law.  Neither the optimizer-containment condition nor a primitive theorem yielding uniformly bounded \(L_n\) is proved here; both are separate checkable hypotheses.  The proposition concerns the positive-definite rank-two restriction only.

defs.def:feasible-ht-pilot-selected-estimator:
Under ass:known-exposure and ass:coordinate-bounded-kappa-feasibility, and using only the independent unpaired pilot, define the regular rank-two selectors
\[
\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}
\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}\widehat w(B),
\qquad
\widehat B_0
\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}}\widehat g_B(0)
\]
by the fixed lexicographic quotient-chart tie-breaking rule.  In the independent main experiment deploy \(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}}^{\mathrm{CV}}\) and \(\widehat\tau_{\widehat B_0}^{\mathrm{CV}}\) through def:observable-coefficient-map.  On this class Zhao's published pseudoinverse equals the ordinary inverse.  The pilot chooses the basis, while the main assignment and main potential-outcome array enter only the displayed estimator.  The existence and measurability of these selectors are derived in thm:pilot-selected-ht-first-order-variance-transfer; no out-of-class fallback is part of the construction.  This construction is the regular deployable restriction, not the primary full-class epsilon-minimizer rule.
defs.def:zhao-rate-admissible-basis-class:
For a fixed \(\overline a\in[1,\infty)\), define
\[
\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}
=\left\{[B]\in\mathcal B_\kappa:
\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
This is the normalized Zhao-rate-admissible class.  The coordinate bound is imposed explicitly and is not inferred from \(\lVert b_a\rVert_2^2=n\).  Its \(\kappa\)-regularity gives \(\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge n\kappa\), so it instantiates the boundedness and nondegeneracy clauses of Zhao's Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\).
defs.def:pilot-plugin:
Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\), and let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the resulting endpoint matrices.  On the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, define the distinct full-class empirical objective
\[
\widehat w_m^+(B)=
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\}\widehat Q_e
\right].
\]
When \(\mathcal B_Z\ne\varnothing\), enumerate all pairs of nonzero rational directions in the finitely many signed pivot charts, normalize each arm direction to squared norm \(n\), retain exactly those block-separable representatives \(B\) for which \(B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\), remove duplicate quotient classes, and reindex the resulting fixed sequence as \((C_k)_{k\ge1}\subset\iota(\mathcal B_Z)\).  For every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable tolerance \(\varepsilon_m\), define
\[
 \rho_m=\inf_{j\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_j),
 \qquad
 \widehat k_m=
 \min\{k\ge1:\widehat w_m^+(C_k)\le\rho_m+\varepsilon_m\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+=C_{\widehat k_m}.
\]
On the compact fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, separately retain
\[
\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\},
\quad
\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\quad
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\]
and retain \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) only as secondary diagnostics.  The measurable positive-tolerance full-carrier selector and the regular rank-two exact argmin are distinct constructions.
defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) denote Zhao's published spectral pseudoinverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and the zero-covariance argmax set may be empty because the rank-stratified pseudoinverse criteria need not attain their extrema across rank changes.  These are criteria induced by Zhao's published unquotiented carrier and expressed on the note's projective quotient; no attainment is built into the definition.
defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\qquad b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  Thus \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, not a projective class named by Zhao.  Its rank-two positive-definite stratum is the image of \(\mathcal B_Z\) under \(\iota\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.
defs.def:robust-objective: The primary robust criterion on the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain is \(w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\}\), with value \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B)\).  On the deployable fixed-threshold rank-two restriction, retain \(w(B)=\max\{\ell_B(c_L),\ell_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}w(B)\).  Retain \(r(B)=\min\{g_B(c_L),g_B(c_U)\}\) and \(v^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}r(B)\) only as secondary regular-class maximin-gain diagnostics.
defs.def:kappa-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_\kappa=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ (\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n),\ \lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), with the predicates ass:block-separable-basis, ass:projective-normalization, and ass:kappa-regularity.
defs.def:observable-coefficient-map:
Define the realized outcome \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(W)\) and Zhao's signed armwise Horvitz--Thompson stack
\[
\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=
\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]
For a representative of \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), define Zhao's published pseudoinverse coefficient
\[
\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)
=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
\]
and the observable control-variate estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}
\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), \((B^{\top}\Omega B)^+=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}\), so these maps reduce to the ordinary-inverse rank-two formulas used by the finite-rate results.  Separately define \(\widehat1_a=n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,a}/\pi_{i,a}\), \(\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)=\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)/\widehat1_a\) when \(\widehat1_a>0\) and zero otherwise, and obtain \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV,SN}}\) by substitution.  No first-order equivalence for the self-normalized variant is asserted.  The expectation identity needed for the oracle comparison is not built into this definition; it is derived from ass:known-exposure in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence.
defs.def:ordinary-intercept-slope-image:
Let
\[
E=\begin{bmatrix}0&I_n\\I_n&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
A_B=\Pi^{-1}\Omega B(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}.
\]
For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\), define the ordinary-domain intercept and slope
\[
a_B=g_B(0),
\qquad
b_B=-n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}(A_BE),
\qquad g_B(c)=a_B+b_Bc,
\]
and define the endpoint drift penalty
\[
p_\xi(b)=\max\{(2/n-b)c_L,(2/n-b)c_U\}.
\]
Whenever the relevant ordinary-domain extrema are attained, put
\[
a^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}a_B,
\quad
\mathcal A_{0,Z}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}a_B,
\quad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B),
\]
\[
\Delta_Z=
\inf_{B_0\in\mathcal A_{0,Z}}w(B_0)
-\inf_{B\in\mathcal B_Z}w(B).
\]
These objects use only the positive-definite ordinary-inverse domain; no singular or Moore--Penrose class is included.
defs.def:zhao-well-defined-ordinary-domain: \(\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z=\{B:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,\ B^{\top}\Omega B\succ0\}\).  This is the unquotiented positive-definite rank-two restriction of Zhao's published pseudoinverse basis domain, not the full published domain.  Define \(q_Z:\widetilde{\mathcal B}_Z\to\mathcal B_Z\) by \(q_Z(B)=[B]\), where \(\mathcal B_Z\) is its quotient by independent nonzero arm-column rescaling.

assumptions.ass:zhao-coordinate-envelope: For every supplied normalized basis, \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), where \(\overline a\ge1\) is fixed along the triangular sequence.

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(G,\nu,(f_i)_{i=1}^n\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and ass:kappa-feasibility, so \(\mathcal B_\kappa\neq\varnothing\).  Under ass:bounded-outcomes and ass:unpaired-pilot, as \(m_1\wedge m_0\to\infty\), \(\sup_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|\to0\) almost surely, \(\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}\to v_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely, and every subsequential limit of \(B_m\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely.  Equivalently, \(\limsup_{m_1,m_0\to\infty}\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}\) almost surely in the projective quotient.

assumptions.ass:bounded-outcomes: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).
assumptions.ass:exposure-positivity: For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
assumptions.ass:frechet-covariance-domain: The feasible covariance image satisfies \(\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)=[c_L,c_U]\).
assumptions.ass:kappa-feasibility: There exist vectors \(b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2=\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2=n\) and \(\lambda_{\min}\{n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B\}\ge\kappa\) for \(B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix}\).
assumptions.ass:unpaired-pilot: The two arm-specific pilot samples are mutually unpaired i.i.d. draws from \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), respectively, and their joint law is independent of \(W\sim\nu\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).

snapshot.stmt: If \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\{B^\star\}\) in the projective quotient, then every measurable selection \(\widehat B\in\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}\) converges almost surely to \(B^\star\).  Without the singleton condition, there exist bounded two-marginal instances satisfying the maintained assumptions for which the outer-set conclusion of thm:plugin-correspondence holds but some measurable plug-in selections fail to converge to a point.

assumptions.ass:unpaired-pilot: The two arm-specific pilot samples are mutually unpaired i.i.d. draws from \(F_1\) and \(F_0\), respectively, and their joint law is independent of \(W\sim\nu\).

snapshot.stmt:
For every rational or real-algebraic moment-complete input \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{cert}}\) satisfying ass:exposure-positivity and every exactly encoded \(\varepsilon>0\), a rank-stratified cylindrical-algebraic procedure terminates and returns rational or real-algebraic bounds and a basis class \([B_\varepsilon]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\) in the note's quotient of Zhao's published carrier satisfying
\[
L_\varepsilon^+\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\le U_\varepsilon^+,
\qquad U_\varepsilon^+-L_\varepsilon^+\le\varepsilon,
\qquad w^+(B_\varepsilon)\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon.
\]
The procedure splits \(\operatorname{rank}(S_B)\in\{0,1,2\}\), represents the pseudoinverse objective by rational semialgebraic formulas on each stratum, and returns a finite checkable CAD sign, sample, and value-isolation certificate covering all strata.  The set \(\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)\le v_{\mathrm{mm}}^++\varepsilon\}\) is nonempty and semialgebraic.  No exact minimizer, outer convergence to \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\), uniform complexity bound, or semidefinite-program reduction is asserted.

defs.def:certified-input-interface: Encode \(\Pi,\Omega,Q(c_L),Q(c_U),c_L,c_U,\kappa,\varepsilon\) either by exact rational or real-algebraic data, or by outward-rounded inclusion oracles supplied with effective refinement moduli and an exact decision oracle for sphere feasibility and the inequality \(\lambda_{\min}(n^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge\kappa\), including equality at the \(\kappa\)-boundary.  Equivalently, the endpoint moment matrices may be encoded through \(\mu_1,\mu_0,\sigma_1^2,\sigma_0^2,c_L,c_U\).  Require \(\varepsilon\) itself to have an exact positive rational or real-algebraic encoding.

 \le
 \inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\widehat w_m^+(B)+\varepsilon_m.
\]

defs.def:pilot-plugin:
Compute the empirical means, variances, and two empirical quantile-coupling covariances from \(\widehat F_1,\widehat F_0\), and let \(\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\) be the resulting endpoint matrices.  On the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published unquotiented all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, define the distinct full-class empirical objective
\[
\widehat w_m^+(B)=
\max_{e\in\{L,U\}}n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[
\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\}\widehat Q_e
\right].
\]
Let
\[
r_\Omega=\max_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}\operatorname{rank}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\in\{0,1,2\}.
\]
A block class has rational support when each nonzero arm column is the squared-norm-\(n\) normalization of a nonzero vector in \(\mathbb Q^n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  In a fixed enumeration of the finitely many signed pivot charts, enumerate all rational-support block classes of rank \(r_\Omega\), remove duplicate quotient classes, and call the resulting sequence \((C_k)_{k\ge1}\).  If \(r_\Omega=0\), take \(C_k=[0]_+\) for every \(k\).  For every finite strictly positive deterministic or pilot-measurable tolerance \(\varepsilon_m\), define
\[
 \rho_m=\inf_{j\ge1}\widehat w_m^+(C_j),
 \qquad
 \widehat k_m=
 \min\{k\ge1:\widehat w_m^+(C_k)\le\rho_m+\varepsilon_m\},
 \qquad
 \widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+=C_{\widehat k_m}.
\]

\[
\widehat w(B)=\max\{\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_L),\widehat\ell_B(\widehat c_U)\},
\quad
\widehat v_{\mathrm{mm}}=\min_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\quad
\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal B_\kappa}\widehat w(B),
\]
and retain \(\widehat r(B)\), \(\widehat v\), and \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_R\) only as secondary diagnostics. \[

\[

\le d_m^+\longrightarrow0

\[

\[

\quad\text{almost surely}.

 \qquad

 |\widehat w_m^+(B)-w^+(B)|,
\]
and let \(\pi_{\min,n}=\min_{i,a}\pi_{i,a}>0\).  For every rank zero, one, or two class \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\),
\[

 \qquad

 \qquad

\]

\[

 w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+

 \le
 8\underline\pi^{-1}n^{\beta-1}\mathbb E_P[M_m]
 +\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_m].

\]

\[

\[

 w^+(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^+)-v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
 \right]\longrightarrow0.
\]

defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:

\[

\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).

defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:

\[

\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain. \]

\[

defs.def:encoded-cad-pilot-selector:
Call a realized pilot input algebraically encoded when \(\Pi,\Omega,\widehat Q_L,\widehat Q_U\), all scalar endpoint fields needed to construct the empirical moment matrices, and a strictly positive tolerance \(\varepsilon_m\) have exact rational or real-algebraic encodings.  Denote it by \(\widehat{\mathfrak I}_{m,\mathrm{alg}}^+\). [\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}]_+,
\widehat L_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+},
\widehat U_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+},
\widehat{\mathscr S}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD}},
\widehat{\mathscr P}_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}
\right).
\]

\[
\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}}
=(\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+})^{\top}
\Omega\widehat B_{m,\varepsilon_m}^{\mathrm{CAD},+}.
\]

\[

+\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}}),
\]
exact real-algebraic representations of its distinct roots with multiplicities, rational isolating intervals for every positive root, exact zero tags, and exact sign certificates for
\[

\begin{cases}
0,&\operatorname{tr}(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})=0,\\
1,&\operatorname{tr}(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})>0
\text{ and }\det(\widehat S_m^{\mathrm{CAD}})=0,\\

\end{cases}
\]

\[
\Gamma_{n,r}=\frac1{\pi_{\min,n}}
\sqrt{\frac{2s_n}{\lambda_r}},
\qquad
T_{n,r}=\frac1n\{\pi_{\min,n}^{-1}
+\overline a\Gamma_{n,r}\},
\]
\[
R_{n,r}^{\mathrm{ad}}
=4\mathfrak M_{4,n}U_{n,r}^2X_n^2
+4\mathfrak M_{3,n}T_{n,r}U_{n,r}X_n.
\]
Then, for every fixed bounded potential-outcome array,
\[
\left|\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}\mid Y)
-\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or},+}\mid Y)\right|
\le R_{n,r}^{\mathrm{ad}}.
\]
The oracle variance is exactly
\[
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or},+}\mid Y)
=n^{-2}Y^{\top}\left\{\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}
-\Pi^{-1}\Omega B S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\right\}Y.
\]
Under ass:iid-potential-pairs,
\[
\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{or},+}\mid Y)
=\ell_B^+(c_H).
\]

If a pilot-measurable selected class \(\widetilde B\) is independent of the main experiment under ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence, the same finite bound holds conditionally with its realized rank.  In particular,
\[
\left|\mathbb E_P\mathbb E_{H^{\otimes n}}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu(\widehat\tau_{\widetilde B}^{\mathrm{CV}}
\mid\widetilde B,Y)
-\mathbb E_P\ell_{\widetilde B}^+(c_H)\right|
\le\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf1\{\operatorname{rank}(S_{\widetilde B})>0\}
R_{n,\operatorname{rank}(S_{\widetilde B})}^{\mathrm{ad}}
\right].
\]
If ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate and ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate hold, then
\[
s_n\le d_n\le\overline d n^\alpha,
\qquad
\mathfrak M_{4,n}\le64(2n)^2d_n^2,
\qquad
\mathfrak M_{3,n}\le8(2n)d_n^2.
\]
For fixed positive lower bounds on \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\) and fixed \(\overline a\), a finite constant \(K_{\mathrm{ad}}\), independent of the selected basis, its positive rank, the bounded array, and \(H\), satisfies
\[
R_{n,r}^{\mathrm{ad}}
\le K_{\mathrm{ad}}
\{n^{4\alpha+4\beta-2}
+n^{(7/2)\alpha+3\beta-2}\},
\qquad r\in\{1,2\}.
\]
Under ass:zhao-first-order-rate, \(\sup_{r\in\{1,2\}}nR_{n,r}^{\mathrm{ad}}\to0\).  At rank two, \(\mathcal S_{2,n}(\kappa,\overline a)=\iota(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a})\), and the ordinary-inverse bridge in \(\texttt{lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence}\) is recovered.  Rank one requires the displayed positive-eigenvalue margin and moment/dependency rates.

Writing
\[
S(b_1,b_0)=
\begin{bmatrix}
b_1^{\top}\Omega_{11}b_1&b_1^{\top}\Omega_{10}b_0\\
b_0^{\top}\Omega_{01}b_1&b_0^{\top}\Omega_{00}b_0
\end{bmatrix},
\]
the exact design-side rank certificates are
\[
r_\Omega=2\Longleftrightarrow
\exists b_1,b_0:\det S(b_1,b_0)>0,
\]
\[
r_\Omega\ge1\Longleftrightarrow
\exists a\in\{1,0\},\ \exists b_a:
b_a^{\top}\Omega_{aa}b_a>0,
\]
\[
r_\Omega=1\Longleftrightarrow r_\Omega\ge1
\text{ and }\det S(b_1,b_0)=0\text{ for all }b_1,b_0,
\]
\[
r_\Omega=0\Longleftrightarrow\Omega_{11}=\Omega_{00}=0.
\]
For an individual class, ranks zero, one, and two are certified respectively by \(\operatorname{tr}(S_B)=0\), \(\det(S_B)=0<\operatorname{tr}(S_B)\), and \(\det(S_B)>0\).  No uniform bridge over uncontrolled rank changes, stability at a vanishing positive eigenvalue, or rank-zero gain is asserted.

defs.def:completion-pseudoinverse-loss:
For \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), let \(S_B^+\) denote Zhao's published spectral pseudoinverse of \(S_B=B^{\top}\Omega B\), and define
\[
g_B^+(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}\!\left[S_B^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B\right],
\qquad \ell_B^+(c)=h(c)-g_B^+(c),
\]
\[
w^+(B)=\max\{\ell_B^+(c_L),\ell_B^+(c_U)\},
\qquad v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+:=\inf_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}w^+(B),
\]
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+
=\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:w^+(B)=v_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\},
\qquad \mathcal A_0^+=\operatorname*{argmax}_{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+}g_B^+(0).
\]
The equality set \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}}^+\) and the zero-covariance argmax set may be empty because the rank-stratified pseudoinverse criteria need not attain their extrema across rank changes.  These are criteria induced by Zhao's published unquotiented carrier and expressed on the note's projective quotient; no attainment is built into the definition.
defs.def:zhao-published-pseudoinverse-domain:
Under Zhao's convention that the inverse of every symmetric positive-semidefinite matrix is obtained by taking spectral reciprocals on positive eigenvalues and assigning zero to zero eigenvalues, Zhao's published unquotiented domain consists of all block-separable matrices
\[
B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\qquad b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n,
\]
including ranks zero, one, and two.  Define \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) to be the note's exact scale-invariant projective quotient of that unquotiented domain.  Two representatives are equivalent when, separately in each arm, both corresponding columns are zero or one is a nonzero scalar multiple of the other.  Each class is represented with every nonzero arm column having squared norm \(n\), while a zero arm remains zero.  Thus \(\mathcal B_Z^+\) is the note's projective quotient of Zhao's published all-block-separable pseudoinverse domain, not a projective class named by Zhao.  Its rank-two positive-definite stratum is the image of \(\mathcal B_Z\) under \(\iota\).
defs.def:zhao-basis-class: \(\mathcal B_Z=\{[B]:B=\begin{bmatrix}b_1&0\\0&b_0\end{bmatrix},\ \lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)>0,\ b_1,b_0\in\mathbb R^n\}\), where \([B]\) quotients independent nonzero rescaling of the two columns and the predicates are ass:block-separable-basis and ass:basis-invertibility.
defs.def:gain-loss: For \(B\in\mathcal B_Z\) and \(c\in\mathcal C(F_1,F_0)\), define the uncontrolled ex ante variance \(h(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[\Pi^{-1}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)]\), the control-variate gain \(g_B(c)=n^{-2}\operatorname{tr}[S_B^{-1}B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}Q(c)\Pi^{-1}\Omega B]\), and the residual variance \(\ell_B(c)=h(c)-g_B(c)\), all in \([0,\infty)\).
defs.def:observable-coefficient-map:
Define the realized outcome \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i(W)\) and Zhao's signed armwise Horvitz--Thompson stack
\[
\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=
\left(\frac{D_{1,1}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,1}},\ldots,
\frac{D_{n,1}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,1}},
-\frac{D_{1,0}Y_1^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{1,0}},\ldots,
-\frac{D_{n,0}Y_n^{\mathrm{obs}}}{\pi_{n,0}}\right)^{\top}.
\]
For a representative of \([B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+\), define Zhao's published pseudoinverse coefficient
\[
\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)
=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^+B^{\top}\Omega\Pi^{-1}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
\]
and the observable control-variate estimator
\[
\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV}}
=n^{-1}\mathbf1^{\top}\widehat Y^{\mathrm{obs}}
-\widehat\gamma^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)^{\top}
\{n^{-1}B^{\top}D-\mathbb E_\nu[n^{-1}B^{\top}D]\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), \((B^{\top}\Omega B)^+=(B^{\top}\Omega B)^{-1}\), so these maps reduce to the ordinary-inverse rank-two formulas used by the finite-rate results.  Separately define \(\widehat1_a=n^{-1}\sum_iD_{i,a}/\pi_{i,a}\), \(\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{SN}}(B)=\widehat\gamma_a^{\mathrm{HT}}(B)/\widehat1_a\) when \(\widehat1_a>0\) and zero otherwise, and obtain \(\widehat\tau_B^{\mathrm{CV,SN}}\) by substitution.  No first-order equivalence for the self-normalized variant is asserted.  The expectation identity needed for the oracle comparison is not built into this definition; it is derived from ass:known-exposure in lem:uniform-zhao-ht-oracle-variance-equivalence.
defs.def:zhao-rate-admissible-basis-class:
For a fixed \(\overline a\in[1,\infty)\), define
\[
\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}
=\left\{[B]\in\mathcal B_\kappa:
\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
This is the normalized Zhao-rate-admissible class.  The coordinate bound is imposed explicitly and is not inferred from \(\lVert b_a\rVert_2^2=n\).  Its \(\kappa\)-regularity gives \(\lambda_{\min}(B^{\top}\Omega B)\ge n\kappa\), so it instantiates the boundedness and nondegeneracy clauses of Zhao's Assumption 2\(^{\dagger}\).
defs.def:rank-adaptive-stability-strata:
Put \(N=2n\), write \(\pi=\mathbb E_\nu D\), and define the centered design vector
\[
Z=D-\pi.
\]
The exact finite-design moment moduli are
\[
\mathfrak M_{4,n}
=\max_{q\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\]
and
\[
\mathfrak M_{3,n}
=\max_{q,r,s\in\{-1,1\}^{N}}
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|.
\]
They are computable from the known finite assignment law by respectively \(2^N\) and \(2^{3N}\) finite evaluations.  Convexity for the fourth moment and separate linearity for the third mixed moment give, for arbitrary real vectors,
\[
\mathbb E_\nu(q^{\top}Z)^4
\le\mathfrak M_{4,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty^4,
\]
\[
\left|\mathbb E_\nu\{(q^{\top}Z)(r^{\top}Z)(s^{\top}Z)\}\right|
\le\mathfrak M_{3,n}\lVert q\rVert_\infty
\lVert r\rVert_\infty\lVert s\rVert_\infty.
\]
Define the exact covariance-support and dependency-neighborhood quantities
\[
s_n=\max_{1\le j\le N}\#\{k:\Omega_{kj}\ne0\},
\qquad
d_n=\max_{1\le j\le N}\#N_{\mathcal G_n}[j].
\]
Whenever \(\mathcal G_n\) is a dependency graph for \(D\), \(s_n\le d_n\).

For a normalized representative \(B\) of a class in \(\mathcal B_Z^+\), put
\[
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}
=\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|.
\]
For \(r\in\{1,2\}\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(\overline a\ge1\), define
\[
\mathcal S_{r,n}(\lambda,\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:
\operatorname{rank}(S_B)=r,\ 
\lambda_+(S_B)\ge n\lambda,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\},
\]
where \(\lambda_+(S_B)\) is the smallest strictly positive eigenvalue.  Define
\[
\mathcal S_{0,n}(\overline a)
=\left\{[B]_+\in\mathcal B_Z^+:S_B=0,\ 
\lVert B\rVert_{\max}\le\overline a\right\}.
\]
No positive-eigenvalue condition is imposed at rank zero.  These strata neither identify nearby classes across ranks nor impose stability as \(\lambda_+(S_B)\downarrow0\).

assumptions.ass:bounded-outcomes: The law \(H\) assigns probability one to \([0,1]^2\).
assumptions.ass:exposure-positivity: For every unit \(i\) and label \(a\in\mathbb A\), \(\pi_{i,a}>0\).
assumptions.ass:iid-potential-pairs: The \(n\) pairs \((Y_i(1),Y_i(0))\) have joint law \(H^{\otimes n}\).
assumptions.ass:known-exposure: For every unit \(i\) and assignments \(w,w'\in\{0,1\}^n\), \(f_i(w)=f_i(w')\) implies \(Y_i(w)=Y_i(w')\).
assumptions.ass:pilot-main-outcome-independence: The sigma-field generated by the two unpaired pilot samples is independent of the sigma-field generated jointly by \(W\) and the main potential-outcome array \(\{(Y_i(1),Y_i(0)):1\le i\le n\}\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-dependency-neighborhood-rate: There is a dependency graph \(\mathcal G_n\) for the \(2n\) coordinates of \(D\): whenever two disjoint coordinate sets have no edge between them, their indicator subvectors are independent under \(\nu\); and there are constants \(\overline d<\infty\) and \(\alpha\ge0\), independent of \(n\), such that every closed graph neighborhood has size at most \(\overline d n^{\alpha}\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-exposure-probability-rate: There are constants \(\underline\pi>0\) and \(\beta\ge0\), independent of \(n\), such that \(\min_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}\pi_{i,a}\ge\underline\pi n^{-\beta}\).
assumptions.ass:projective-normalization: The ordered norm pair satisfies \((\lVert b_1\rVert_2^2,\lVert b_0\rVert_2^2)=(n,n)\).
assumptions.ass:zhao-coordinate-envelope: For every supplied normalized basis, \(\max_{1\le i\le n,\,a\in\{1,0\}}|b_{a,i}|\le\overline a\), where \(\overline a\ge1\) is fixed along the triangular sequence.

snapshot.stmt:
Let \(\mathcal K=\mathcal B_{\kappa,\overline a}\), let \(\mathcal Z\) be the normalized positive-definite rank-two carrier, put \(a(B)=g_B(0)\),
\[
a^\star=\max_{B\in\mathcal K}a(B),
\quad
A_0=\operatorname*{argmax}_{B\in\mathcal K}a(B),
\quad
v=\min_{B\in\mathcal K}w(B),
\quad
A_{\mathrm{mm}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{B\in\mathcal K}w(B),
\quad
q=\inf_{B\in A_0}w(B).
\]
Fix the finite signed-pivot charts and their semialgebraic quotient distance \(d_{\mathrm{pr}}\).  A primitive geometry record \(\mathscr G_{\mathrm{CAD}}\) consists of exact rational or real-algebraic CAD, KKT, and interval-Hessian certificates with the following components.

First, for some \(\zeta_0,\zeta_{\mathrm{mm}}>0\), it certifies the strict inside/outside gaps
\[
\sup_{B\in\mathcal Z\setminus\mathcal K}a(B)
\le a^\star-\zeta_0,
\qquad
\inf_{B\in\mathcal Z\setminus\mathcal K}w(B)
\ge v+\zeta_{\mathrm{mm}}.
\tag{G1}
\]
Second, it gives a finite semialgebraic stratified chart cover of \(A_0\), exact nominal KKT multipliers, linear independence of the active constraint gradients, strictly positive multipliers for active inequalities, and a strictly negative reduced Hessian for the nominal Lagrangian.  On
\[
A_q=\{C\in A_0:w(C)=q\},
\]
it additionally gives exact weights \(\theta_L(C),\theta_U(C)\ge0\), summing to one and supported only on endpoint losses attaining \(w(C)\), such that the weighted endpoint gradient plus the certified active-constraint multipliers has the feasible normal sign.  It gives uniform algebraic bounds on the endpoint Hessians and Taylor remainders and a positive \(w\)-gap on \(A_0\setminus A_q\).  These finite primitives certify constants \(\rho,\mu>0\) and \(M<\infty\) for the Taylor conclusions
\[
a^\star-a(B)\ge\mu d_{\mathrm{pr}}(B,A_0)^2,
\qquad
[q-w(B)]_+\le M d_{\mathrm{pr}}(B,A_0)^2
\quad\text{when }d_{\mathrm{pr}}(B,A_0)\le\rho.
\tag{G2}
\]
Third, on the compact away set \(d_{\mathrm{pr}}(B,A_0)\ge\rho\), it certifies
\[
a^\star-a(B)\ge\gamma>0,
\qquad
[q-w(B)]_+\le R<\infty.
\tag{G3}
\]

Every valid \(\mathscr G_{\mathrm{CAD}}\) proves
\[
\mathcal A_{0,Z}=A_0,
\qquad
\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm},Z}=A_{\mathrm{mm}},
\]
and derives, rather than assumes, the global error bound
\[
[q-w(B)]_+
\le L\{a^\star-a(B)\}
\quad(B\in\mathcal K),
\qquad
L=\max\{M/\mu,R/\gamma\}.
\tag{G4}
\]
Consequently, if
\[
e=\sup_{\mathcal K}|\widehat g_B(0)-g_B(0)|,
\qquad
d=\sup_{\mathcal K}|\widehat w(B)-w(B)|,
\]
then any empirical nominal maximizer \(\widehat B_0\) and robust minimizer \(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}}\) satisfy
\[
w(\widehat B_0)\ge q-2Le,
\qquad
w(\widehat B_{\mathrm{mm}})\le v+2d.
\]
If their observable-versus-oracle variance errors are bounded by \(R_0\) and \(R_{\mathrm{mm}}\), respectively, then
\[
V_0-V_{\mathrm{mm}}
\ge(q-v)-2Le-2d-R_0-R_{\mathrm{mm}}.
\tag{G5}
\]
Thus containment and the finite comparison constant are consequences of exact primitive certificates, not maintained hypotheses.

\[

snapshot.stmt:
For the exact triangle instance in \(\texttt{thm:triangle-completion-separation-certificate}\), take \(\kappa=1/8\), \(\overline a=2\), and define
\[
x=\sqrt{\frac32}(1,-1,0)^{\top},
\qquad
y_0=\frac1{\sqrt2}(1,1,-2)^{\top},
\]
\[
t=\frac{\sqrt{3410}}{110}+\frac{2\sqrt{330}}{55},
\qquad
u=-\frac{\sqrt{3410}}{55}+\frac{2\sqrt{330}}{55},
\qquad
y_R=(t,t,u)^{\top}.
\]
Let \(B_0=B(x,y_0)\) and \(B_R=B(x,y_R)\).  Exact CAD sign and equality certificates verify
\[
B_0\in\mathcal A_0,
\qquad
B_R\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{mm}},
\qquad
\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_{B_0})
=\lambda_{\min}(3^{-1}S_{B_R})=\frac4{27}>\frac18.
\]
Take the realized unpaired pilot samples in both arms to be \((0,1)\).  Then the empirical marginals, endpoint matrices, and population endpoint matrices agree exactly, so the two pilot objective errors are zero and the input is rational or real algebraic.

For the observable estimator in \(\texttt{def:observable-coefficient-map}\), exact enumeration of all eight assignments and all eight endpoint potential-outcome arrays gives
\[
V_{0,L}=\frac{3112847}{480000},
\qquad
V_{0,U}=\frac{1019349}{160000},
\]
\[
V_{R,L}
=\frac{948747698543}{133309920000}
-\frac{9641367\sqrt{93}}{44795000},
\]
\[
V_{R,U}
=\frac{304083944181}{44436640000}
-\frac{8821467\sqrt{93}}{44795000}.
\]
The lower covariance endpoint is worst for both displayed bases.  Hence the observable robust-versus-zero variance gap is
\[
G_{\mathrm{obs}}
=V_{0,L}-V_{R,L}
=-\frac{87728973}{138864500}
+\frac{9641367\sqrt{93}}{44795000}>0.
\]
The exact objective gap is
\[
\delta=\frac{521}{1200}-\frac{2613}{8432}
